```
uint32_t gba_read32(GBA *g, uint32_t addr) {
    switch (addr >> 24) {
    case 0x00: return rd32_al(g->bios + (addr & 0x3FFC));
    case 0x02: return rd32_al(g->ewram + (addr & 0x3FFFC));
    case 0x03: return rd32_al(g->iwram + (addr & 0x7FFC));
    case 0x04: return io_read16(g, addr) | ((uint32_t)io_read16(g, addr + 2) << 16);
    case 0x05: return rd32_al(g->pal + (addr & 0x3FC));
    case 0x06: return rd32_al(g->vram + (addr & 0x17FFC));
    case 0x07: return rd32_al(g->oam + (addr & 0x3FC));
    case 0x08: case 0x09: case 0x0A: case 0x0B: case 0x0C: case 0x0D: {
        if (eeprom_addr_in_range(g, addr)) return 0;  /* EEPROM reads are bit-serial via DMA */
        uint32_t off = (addr - 0x08000000) & (g->rom_mask & ~3u);
        return off < g->rom_size ? rd32_al(g->rom + off) : 0;
    }
    case 0x0E: return rd32_al(g->save_mem + (addr & 0x1FFFC));
    default: return 0;
    }
}
```

```
/*
 * ppu.c - GBA background/sprite rendering (modes 0-5, OBJ).
 * Clean-room implementation of the GBA PPU, following the GBATEK
 * description of the display controller.
 */
#include "gba.h"
#include "mem.h"

static inline uint16_t read_pal(GBA *g, int idx) {
    idx &= 0x1FF;
    return (uint16_t)(g->pal[idx*2] | (g->pal[idx*2+1] << 8));
}
static inline uint16_t read_vram16(GBA *g, uint32_t off) {
    off &= 0x1FFFF;
    return (uint16_t)(g->vram[off] | (g->vram[off+1] << 8));
}
static inline uint8_t read_vram8(GBA *g, uint32_t off) {
    return g->vram[off & 0x1FFFF];
}

/* Render a full scanline y (0..159) into ppu.frame */
static void render_line(GBA *g, int y) {
    Ppu *p = &g->ppu;
    uint16_t dispcnt = p->dispcnt;
    int bg_mode = dispcnt & 0x7;
    bool obj_enabled = dispcnt & 0x1000;
    uint32_t base = (uint32_t)y * SCREEN_W;

    /* backdrop */
    uint16_t backdrop = read_pal(g, 0);
```

```
/*
 * gba.c - GBA system core: init/reset, ROM load, frame loop, timing.
 * Clean-room implementation.
 */
#include "gba.h"
#include "mem.h"
#include "arm.h"
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

static const uint8_t builtin_bios[BIOS_SIZE] = {0};   /* zeros OK: many titles boot */

void gba_init(GBA *g) {
    memset(g, 0, sizeof(GBA));
    g->frameskip = 0;
    g->throttle = 60;
    g->bios_enabled = true;
```

```
static void swi_intr_wait(GBA *g) {
    /* SWI 0x04: wait for any of the IRQs in r0; r1=1 discards old flags.

    g->cst.halt = true;
```

```
    a->cur = (a->cur + 1) % AUDIO_FRAGS;
}
```

```
/* Run one video frame: step the PPU line by line, running the CPU for the
 * cycles each scanline takes, firing HBlank/VBlank/VCount interrupts. */
static void run_frame_core(GBA *g) {
    const uint32_t line_cycles = 1232;      /* 240px @ 4 cyc + hblank */

    for (int line = 0; line < 228; line++) {
        g->ppu.vcount = (uint16_t)line;

        /* VBlank: start (line 160) sets IF and wakes the CPU */
        if (line == 160) {
            if (g->ppu.dispstat & 0x0008) g->if_reg |= IF_VBLANK;
            ppu_render_frame(g);
            g->frame_count++;
            if (g->cst.halt) g->cst.halt = false;   /* VBlankIntrWait satisfied */
            dma_trigger(g, 1);                      /* VBlank-scheduled DMA */
        }

        /* render visible lines lazily (all at VBlank, already done above) */

        /* HBlank IRQ at the start of each line's blanking period */
        if (g->ppu.dispstat & 0x0010) g->if_reg |= IF_HBLANK;
        if (line < 160) dma_trigger(g, 2);          /* HBlank-scheduled DMA */

        /* VCount match IRQ */
        if (g->ppu.dispstat & 0x0020) {
            int vm = (g->ppu.dispstat >> 8) & 0xFF;
            if (line == vm) g->if_reg |= IF_VCOUNT;
        }

        io_update_timers(g, line_cycles);

        /* Run the CPU for this scanline's cycles (interrupts handled inside) */
        arm_execute(g, line_cycles);
    }
    g->ppu.vcount = 0;
}

void gba_run_frame(GBA *g) {
    run_frame_core(g);
}
```

```
/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
/* public loop                                                         */
/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
void arm_execute(GBA *g, uint32_t max_cycles) {
    uint32_t start = g->cycle;
    while (g->cycle - start < max_cycles) {
        /* IRQ exception has priority over halt. IF is NOT acknowledged here:
         * the GBA leaves the flag set so the handler can read IE&IF to find
         * the source; the BIOS/handler clears it by writing 1 to IF. */
        if (g->ime && (g->if_reg & g->ie & 0x3FFF) && !(g->cpu.cpsr & CPSR_I)) {
            g->cst.halt = false;   /* an enabled IRQ wakes the CPU from Halt */
            enter_exception(g, 0x12, g->cpu.r[15] + (thumb_mode(g) ? 2 : 4), 0x18);
            continue;
        }
        if (g->cst.halt) {
            /* CPU asleep: just burn cycles until the scanline/frame budget ends */
            g->cycle = start + max_cycles;
            break;
        }
        if (thumb_mode(g)) thumb_exec(g);
        else arm_exec(g);
    }
```

```
#include "gba.h"
#include "headless/input_script.h"
#include <stdio.h>

/* Run `frames` frames on `gba` via gba_run_frame, writing one line per frame to
   `hash_out` in the format "%d %08x\n": 0-based frame index, a space, and 8
   lowercase hex digits of the FNV-1a framebuffer hash.

   If `script` is non-NULL, its events for frame i are applied to gba->input
   before frame i runs. If `before_frame` is non-NULL it is called after that,
   just before the frame runs; if `on_frame` is non-NULL it is called after each
   frame. Both get `ctx`.

   Returns 0 on success, non-zero on I/O failure (e.g. fprintf returns negative)
   or if `frames` is negative.

   The caller owns `hash_out` — it opens and closes the stream. This function
   does not flush; call fflush or close to force the writes to disk. */
int headless_run(GBA* gba, int frames, FILE* hash_out, InputScript* script,
                 void (*before_frame)(GBA* gba, void* ctx), void (*on_frame)(GBA* gba, void* ctx),
                 void* ctx);

#endif // HEADLESS_HEADLESS_H
```

```
/* Run lines 0..159 of frame 4, then set VBlank IF and single-step. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include "gba.h"
#include "mem.h"
#include "arm.h"

static void run_line(GBA *g, int line) {
    g->ppu.vcount = line;
    if (g->ppu.dispstat & 0x10) g->if_reg |= IF_HBLANK;
    if (g->ppu.dispstat & 0x20) { int vm = (g->ppu.dispstat >> 8) & 0xFF; if (line == vm) g->if_reg |= IF_VCOUNT; }
    io_update_timers(g, 1232);
    arm_execute(g, 1232);
}

int main(int argc, char **argv) {
    GBA *g = calloc(1, sizeof(GBA));
    gba_init(g);
    gba_load_bios(g, argv[2]);
    gba_load_rom(g, argv[1]);
    gba_reset(g);

    for (int f = 1; f <= 3; f++) gba_run_frame(g);

    for (int line = 0; line < 160; line++) run_line(g, line);

    /* Now do the VBlank line by hand. */
    g->ppu.vcount = 160;
    if (g->ppu.dispstat & 0x8) g->if_reg |= IF_VBLANK;
    ppu_render_frame(g); g->frame_count++;
    if (g->cst.halt) g->cst.halt = false;
    printf("IF=%04X IE=%04X IME=%d cpsr=%08X pc=%08X flag=%04X\n",
        g->if_reg, g->ie, g->ime, g->cpu.cpsr, g->cpu.r[15], gba_read16(g, 0x030022DC));

    for (int s = 0; s < 900; s++) {
        uint32_t pc = g->cpu.r[15];
        printf("s%-3d pc=%08X IF=%04X flag=%04X cpsr=%08X lr=%08X%s\n",
            s, pc, g->if_reg, gba_read16(g, 0x030022DC), g->cpu.cpsr, g->cpu.r[14],
            (pc==0x18?"  <<IRQ":""));
        arm_execute(g, 1);
    }
    return 0;
}
```

```
}
```

```
void gba_swi(GBA *g, uint32_t comment) {
    uint32_t swi_num = comment & 0xFF;

    /* Advance the program counter past the SWI instruction before running
       the handler. Handlers such as Halt/IntrWait set cst.halt, which the
       frame loop then uses to sleep the CPU until the next interrupt. */
    if (thumb_mode_p(g)) g->cpu.r[15] += 2;
    else                 g->cpu.r[15] += 4;
```

```
void gba_write8(GBA *g, uint32_t addr, uint8_t v) {
    switch (addr >> 24) {
    case 0x02: g->ewram[addr & 0x3FFFF] = v; return;
    case 0x03: g->iwram[addr & 0x7FFF] = v; return;
    case 0x04: {
                 /* HALTCNT (0x04000301). The BIOS Halt/IntrWait loops write
                    it to suspend the CPU until an IRQ arrives; without it the
                    BIOS never reaches the cartridge. */
                 if ((addr & 0x0FFFFFFF) == 0x00000301) {
                     g->io[0x301] = v;
                     g->cst.halt = true;
                     if (v == 0x80) g->cst.stopped = true;
                     return;
                 }
                 uint16_t cur = io_read16(g, addr & ~1u);
                 if (addr & 1) cur = (uint16_t)((cur & 0x00FF) | (v << 8));
                 else cur = (uint16_t)((cur & 0xFF00) | v);
                 io_write16(g, addr & ~1u, cur); return; }
    case 0x05: g->pal[addr & 0x3FF] = v; return;
    case 0x06: g->vram[addr & 0x17FFF] = v; return;
    case 0x07: g->oam[addr & 0x3FF] = v; return;
    case 0x0D: return;
```

```
739:void arm_execute(GBA *g, uint32_t max_cycles) {
void arm_execute(GBA *g, uint32_t max_cycles) {
    uint32_t start = g->cycle;
    while (g->cycle - start < max_cycles) {
        /* IRQ exception has priority over halt. IF is NOT acknowledged here:
         * the GBA leaves the flag set so the handler can read IE&IF to find
         * the source; the BIOS/handler clears it by writing 1 to IF. */
        if (g->ime && (g->if_reg & g->ie & 0x3FFF) && !(g->cpu.cpsr & CPSR_I)) {
            g->cst.halt = false;   /* an enabled IRQ wakes the CPU from Halt */
            enter_exception(g, 0x12, g->cpu.r[15] + (thumb_mode(g) ? 2 : 4), 0x18);
            continue;
        }
        if (g->cst.halt) {
            /* CPU asleep: just burn cycles until the scanline/frame budget ends */
            g->cycle = start + max_cycles;
            break;
        }
        if (thumb_mode(g)) thumb_exec(g);
        else arm_exec(g);
    }
}

void arm_raise_interrupt(GBA *g, int line) { (void)g; (void)line; }
void arm_set_irq_line(GBA *g, bool high) { g->cst.irq_pending = high; }
bool arm_is_halted(GBA *g) { return g->cst.halt; }
```

```
ReimplementaciĂłn limpia del emulador GBA BoycottAdvance 0.2.8 (C).
El usuario se comunica en espaĂ±ol. Repo privado `Dragonfire51/BoycottAdvance-Reborn`.

## Documentación de referencia (OBLIGATORIA)

**Usar SIEMPRE GBATEK como referencia** para corregir bugs y añadir implementaciones:
<https://problemkaputt.de/gbatek.htm> (texto plano: <https://problemkaputt.de/gbatek.txt>).

registros LCD/sonido/DMA/timers/interrupciones, opcodes ARM/THUMB, funciones BIOS.
Antes de tocar el núcleo, comprobar el comportamiento contra GBATEK y citar la sección.
```

```
void gba_write16(GBA *g, uint32_t addr, uint16_t v) {
    switch (addr >> 24) {
    case 0x02: wr16_al(g->ewram + (addr & 0x3FFFE), v); return;
    case 0x03: wr16_al(g->iwram + (addr & 0x7FFE), v); return;
    case 0x04: io_write16(g, addr, v); return;
    case 0x05: wr16_al(g->pal + (addr & 0x3FE), v); return;
    case 0x06: wr16_al(g->vram + (addr & 0x17FFE), v); return;
    case 0x07: wr16_al(g->oam + (addr & 0x3FE), v); return;
    case 0x0D:
        if (eeprom_addr_in_range(g, addr)) {   /* one protocol bit per halfword */
            eeprom_write_bit(g, (uint8_t)(v & 1));
            if (g->eeprom.dirty) { g->save_dirty = true; g->eeprom.dirty = false; }
        }
        return;
    case 0x0E: wr16_al(g->save_mem + (addr & 0x1FFFE), v); return;
    default: return;
    }
}
```

```
=== io_write8 / byte path ===
void gba_write8(GBA *g, uint32_t addr, uint8_t v) {
    switch (addr >> 24) {
    case 0x02: g->ewram[addr & 0x3FFFF] = v; return;
    case 0x03: g->iwram[addr & 0x7FFF] = v; return;
    case 0x04: {
                 /* HALTCNT (0x04000301). The BIOS Halt/IntrWait loops write
                    it to suspend the CPU until an IRQ arrives; without it the
                    BIOS never reaches the cartridge. */
                 if ((addr & 0x0FFFFFFF) == 0x00000301) {
                     g->io[0x301] = v;
                     g->cst.halt = true;
                     if (v == 0x80) g->cst.stopped = true;
                     return;
                 }
                 uint16_t cur = io_read16(g, addr & ~1u);
                 if (addr & 1) cur = (uint16_t)((cur & 0x00FF) | (v << 8));
                 else cur = (uint16_t)((cur & 0xFF00) | v);
                 io_write16(g, addr & ~1u, cur); return; }
    case 0x05: g->pal[addr & 0x3FF] = v; return;
    case 0x06: g->vram[addr & 0x17FFF] = v; return;
    case 0x07: g->oam[addr & 0x3FF] = v; return;
    case 0x0D: return;
    case 0x0E: g->save_mem[addr & 0x1FFFF] = v; return;
    default: return;
    }
}
```

```
/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
/* public loop                                                         */
/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
void arm_execute(GBA *g, uint32_t max_cycles) {
    uint32_t start = g->cycle;
    while (g->cycle - start < max_cycles) {
        /* A halted CPU wakes as soon as an *enabled* interrupt is requested
           (IE & IF), regardless of IME or the CPSR I bit; IME only gates the
           exception vectoring below. Missing this stalls the CPU until the
           next VBlank and desynchronises code that polls VCOUNT. */
        if (g->cst.halt && (g->if_reg & g->ie & 0x3FFF)) g->cst.halt = false;

        /* IRQ exception has priority over halt. IF is NOT acknowledged here:
         * the GBA leaves the flag set so the handler can read IE&IF to find
         * the source; the BIOS/handler clears it by writing 1 to IF. */
        if (g->ime && (g->if_reg & g->ie & 0x3FFF) && !(g->cpu.cpsr & CPSR_I)) {
            g->cst.halt = false;   /* an enabled IRQ wakes the CPU from Halt */
            enter_exception(g, 0x12, g->cpu.r[15] + (thumb_mode(g) ? 2 : 4), 0x18);
            continue;
        }
        if (g->cst.halt) {
            /* CPU asleep: just burn cycles until the scanline/frame budget ends */
            g->cycle = start + max_cycles;
            break;
        }
        if (thumb_mode(g)) thumb_exec(g);
        else arm_exec(g);
    }
}
```

```
void gba_write8(GBA *g, uint32_t addr, uint8_t v) {
    switch (addr >> 24) {
    case 0x02: g->ewram[addr & 0x3FFFF] = v; return;
    case 0x03: g->iwram[addr & 0x7FFF] = v; return;
    case 0x04: {
                 /* HALTCNT (0x04000301). The BIOS Halt/IntrWait loops write
                    it to suspend the CPU until an IRQ arrives; without it the
                    BIOS never reaches the cartridge. */
                 if ((addr & 0x0FFFFFFF) == 0x00000301) {
                     g->io[0x301] = v;
                     g->cst.halt = true;
                     if (v == 0x80) g->cst.stopped = true;
                     return;
                 }
                 uint16_t cur = io_read16(g, addr & ~1u);
                 if (addr & 1) cur = (uint16_t)((cur & 0x00FF) | (v << 8));
                 else cur = (uint16_t)((cur & 0xFF00) | v);
```

```
cd /workspace/BA && git checkout -b fix/bios-halt-haltcnt-and-win32-native && git add -A src/ && git commit -q -m "fix(core): BIOS Halt/IntrWait HALTCNT mask so the BIOS hands off to the ROM
The BIOS Halt / IntrWait helper writes HALTCNT at 0x04000301 to suspend
the CPU, but the address test in gba_write8 masked with 0x0FFFFFFF, which
yields 0x4000301 and never matches 0x301. The write was therefore treated
as an ordinary POSTFLG byte, the CPU never slept, and the BIOS busy-spun
forever in its halt loop instead of jumping to the cartridge. That is why
the screen stayed black right after the logo.
With the mask corrected to 0x00FFFFFF the BIOS reaches the ROM: the
DISPCNT sequence now matches the reference emulator exactly
(0080, 1002 x108, 9802 x101), i.e. the game turns the display on.
Also in this change:
- arm.c: a halted CPU wakes as soon as an enabled IRQ is pending
  (IE & IF), independent of IME and the CPSR I bit.
- gba.c: DISPSTAT reports live VBlank / HBlank / VCount status bits and
  VBlank/HBlank-scheduled DMA is triggered each line.
- mem.c/h: repeat DMA reloads its latched source/destination addresses and
  a dma_trigger() helper runs channels by start timing.
- win32.c: audio shutdown stops the waveOut callback before resetting so
  closing the window no longer leaves the process behind; History shows
  only the current release.
- Bump version to v1.4.6.
```

```
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Install mingw and zip
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y gcc-mingw-w64-i686 gcc-mingw-w64-x86-64 zip
      - name: Build ${{ matrix.arch }} (native, no SDL)
        run: |
          # The Windows build is SDL-free: native GDI/Direct3D 9 video,
          # WinMM (waveOut) audio and a full Win32 menu bar.
          make -f Makefile.win32 ${{ matrix.make_arch }}

          cp boycottadvance-reborn-${{ matrix.arch_name }}.exe dist/boycottadvance-reborn.exe
          cp README.md gba_bios.bin dist/

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: ${{ matrix.arch }}
```

```
  reporting "none". Serial EEPROM is implemented: the 4Kbit/64Kbit chip
  is bit-serial on the D0 line and only reachable through DMA, so the DMA
  transfer count selects the protocol phase (9/17 read address, 68 read
  data, 73/81 write, 1 ready poll) and the address width is locked in on
  the first command. Medabots (Metabee and Rokusho) keep their save on
  EEPROM and used to stall in the backup driver before the title screen.
  Battery saves are now written to `<rom>.sav` on exit and on reset and
  read back when the ROM is opened.
```

```
import json

### The black screen after the logo is fixed
The BIOS \`Halt\` / \`IntrWait\` helper suspends the CPU by writing HALTCNT
at \`0x04000301\`. The address test used the wrong mask
(\`0x0FFFFFFF\` leaves \`0x4000301\`), so the write was treated as an
ordinary byte, the CPU never slept, and the BIOS spun forever in its halt
loop instead of jumping into the cartridge. That is why the screen stayed
black right after the logo.
With the mask corrected to \`0x00FFFFFF\` the BIOS hands off to the ROM.
Verified against a reference emulator: the display-control (DISPCNT)
sequence now matches exactly and the game turns the screen on.
### Also in this release
- A halted CPU wakes as soon as an enabled interrupt is pending
  (\`IE & IF\`), independent of IME and the CPSR I bit.
- DISPSTAT reports the live VBlank / HBlank / VCount status bits.
- DMA channels scheduled for VBlank or HBlank now run at those moments,
  and repeat transfers reload their latched addresses.
- Windows: closing the window no longer leaves the process behind; the
  waveOut callback is stopped before the device is reset.
Windows x86/x64 remains SDL-free: native GDI / Direct3D 9 video, WinMM
audio and the full native menu bar.
"""
```

```
/* mode helpers (banked regs) */
static int bank_of(uint32_t cpsr) {
    switch (cpsr & 0x1F) {
    case 0x11: return BANK_FIQ;
    case 0x12: return BANK_IRQ;
    case 0x13: return BANK_SVC;
    case 0x17: return BANK_ABT;
    case 0x1B: return BANK_UND;
    default:   return BANK_USR;
    }
}

static void change_mode(GBA *g, uint32_t new_cpsr) {
    int ob = bank_of(get_cpsr(g)), nb = bank_of(new_cpsr);
    if (ob == nb) { set_cpsr(g, new_cpsr); return; }
    /* save current mode's r13/r14 into banks */
    g->cpu.bank[ob][5] = g->cpu.r[13];
    g->cpu.bank[ob][6] = g->cpu.r[14];
    /* switch mode, restore r13/r14 of new mode */
    set_cpsr(g, new_cpsr);
    g->cpu.r[13] = g->cpu.bank[nb][5];
    g->cpu.r[14] = g->cpu.bank[nb][6];
}

void arm_set_mode(GBA *g, uint32_t mode) {
    change_mode(g, (get_cpsr(g) & ~0x1F) | mode);
}

    /* Vectors run in ARM state; force IRQ-disable and clear the Thumb bit. */
```

```
/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
/* public loop                                                         */
/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
void arm_execute(GBA *g, uint32_t max_cycles) {
    uint32_t start = g->cycle;
    while (g->cycle - start < max_cycles) {
        /* A halted CPU wakes as soon as an *enabled* interrupt is requested
           (IE & IF), regardless of IME or the CPSR I bit; IME only gates the
           exception vectoring below. Missing this stalls the CPU until the
           next VBlank and desynchronises code that polls VCOUNT. */
        if (g->cst.halt && (g->if_reg & g->ie & 0x3FFF)) g->cst.halt = false;

        /* IRQ exception has priority over halt. IF is NOT acknowledged here:
         * the GBA leaves the flag set so the handler can read IE&IF to find
         * the source; the BIOS/handler clears it by writing 1 to IF. */
        if (g->ime && (g->if_reg & g->ie & 0x3FFF) && !(g->cpu.cpsr & CPSR_I)) {
            g->cst.halt = false;   /* an enabled IRQ wakes the CPU from Halt */
            enter_exception(g, 0x12, g->cpu.r[15] + (thumb_mode(g) ? 2 : 4), 0x18);
            continue;
        }
        if (g->cst.halt) {
            /* CPU asleep: just burn cycles until the scanline/frame budget ends */
            g->cycle = start + max_cycles;
            break;
        }
        if (thumb_mode(g)) thumb_exec(g);
        else arm_exec(g);
    }
}
```

```
    uint32_t swi_num = comment & 0xFF;

    /* Advance the program counter past the SWI instruction before running
       the handler. Handlers such as Halt/IntrWait set cst.halt, which the
       frame loop then uses to sleep the CPU until the next interrupt. */
    if (thumb_mode_p(g)) g->cpu.r[15] += 2;
    else                 g->cpu.r[15] += 4;

    switch (swi_num) {
    case 0x00: swi_soft_reset(g); break;
    case 0x01: swi_register_ram_reset(g); break;
```

```
/*
 * bios.c - GBA BIOS SWI handlers.
 * Clean-room implementation of the classic GBA BIOS calls used to boot games.
 */
#include "gba.h"
#include "mem.h"

static inline bool thumb_mode_p(GBA *g) { return (g->cpu.cpsr & CPSR_T) != 0; }

static void swi_soft_reset(GBA *g) { (void)g; }
static void swi_register_ram_reset(GBA *g) { (void)g; }
static void swi_halt(GBA *g) {
    g->cst.halt = true;
}
static void swi_stop(GBA *g) {
    g->cst.halt = true;
    g->cst.stopped = true;
}
static void swi_intr_wait(GBA *g) {
    /* SWI 0x04: wait for any of the IRQs in r0; r1=1 discards old flags.
       We let the frame loop keep running and only halt the CPU here. */
    g->cst.halt = true;
}
static void swi_vblank_intr_wait(GBA *g) {
    /* SWI 0x05: VBlankIntrWait. Equivalent to IntrWait(1,1).
       Halt until the VBlank IRQ condition is met; the frame loop clears
       halt as soon as IF_VBLANK is raised. */
    g->cst.halt = true;
}
static void swi_div32(GBA *g) {
    int32_t a = (int32_t)g->cpu.r[0];
    int32_t b = (int32_t)g->cpu.r[1];
    if (b == 0) { g->cpu.r[0] = a; g->cpu.r[1] = a; g->cpu.r[3] = 0; return; }
    g->cpu.r[0] = (uint32_t)(a / b);
    g->cpu.r[3] = (uint32_t)(a % b);
    g->cpu.r[1] = (uint32_t)(a % b);
}
static void swi_div_arm(GBA *g) { swi_div32(g); }
```

```
/* Minimal driver for the reference core: run N frames headless and dump a
   PC trace so it can be diffed against our emulator. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include "gba.h"

static FILE *g_pc;
static long  g_pcn;

static void pc_hook(const struct GBA *gba, void *ctx) {
    (void)ctx;
    if (!g_pc) return;
    uint32_t pc = gba->cpu.regs[15] - 4u;   /* executing PC */
    if (g_pcn < 4000000) { fprintf(g_pc, "%08X\n", pc); g_pcn++; }
}

int main(int argc, char **argv) {
    if (argc < 3) { fprintf(stderr, "usage: %s rom bios [frames] [log_from_frame]\n", argv[0]); return 2; }
    int frames = argc > 3 ? atoi(argv[3]) : 400;
    int log_from = argc > 4 ? atoi(argv[4]) : 0;

    GBA *g = calloc(1, sizeof(GBA));
    gba_init(g);
    if (!gba_load_bios(g, argv[2])) { fprintf(stderr, "bios load failed\n"); return 1; }
    if (!gba_load_rom(g, argv[1], NULL)) { fprintf(stderr, "rom load failed\n"); return 1; }

    g_pc = fopen("/workspace/h/ref_pc.txt", "w");

    for (int i = 0; i < frames; i++) {
        if (i == log_from) {
            gba_set_pc_hook(g, 0x082E7DCC, pc_hook, NULL);
        }
        gba_run_frame(g);
    }
    fclose(g_pc);
    printf("done frames=%d pc_hook_hits=%ld DISPCNT=%04X\n",
           frames, g_pcn, g->ppu.dispcnt);
    return 0;
}
```

```
static void swi_halt(ARM7TDMI* cpu) {

/* ======================================================================
 * SWI 0x04 - IntrWait
 * R0 = discard old flags, R1 = interrupt mask to wait for
 * ====================================================================== */
static void swi_intr_wait(ARM7TDMI* cpu) {
    uint32_t discard = cpu->regs[0];
    uint16_t mask = (uint16_t)cpu->regs[1];

    /* The BIOS forces IME on so the wait can complete. */
    bus_write16(cpu->bus, 0x04000208, 1);

    uint16_t flags = bus_read16(cpu->bus, 0x03007FF8);

    if ((discard & 1) && !cpu->in_intr_wait) {
        /* First entry with r0=1: throw away stale flags and wait for a
         * NEW occurrence.  Must not run again on re-entry, or flags set
         * by the IRQ handler while we slept would be discarded too. */
        bus_write16(cpu->bus, 0x03007FF8, flags & ~mask);
    } else if (flags & mask) {
        /* Satisfied: consume only the awaited bits and return. */
        bus_write16(cpu->bus, 0x03007FF8, flags & ~mask);
        cpu->in_intr_wait = false;
        return;
    }
```

```
void gba_swi(GBA *g, uint32_t comment) {
    uint32_t swi_num = comment & 0xFF;

    /* Advance the program counter past the SWI instruction before running
       the handler. Handlers such as Halt/IntrWait set cst.halt, which the
       frame loop then uses to sleep the CPU until the next interrupt. */
    if (thumb_mode_p(g)) g->cpu.r[15] += 2;
    else                 g->cpu.r[15] += 4;

    switch (swi_num) {
    case 0x00: swi_soft_reset(g); break;
    case 0x01: swi_register_ram_reset(g); break;
    case 0x02: swi_halt(g); break;
    case 0x03: swi_stop(g); break;
    case 0x04: swi_intr_wait(g); break;
    case 0x05: swi_vblank_intr_wait(g); break;
    case 0x06: swi_div32(g); break;
    case 0x07: swi_div_arm(g); break;
    case 0x08: swi_sqrt(g); break;
    case 0x0B: swi_cpu_set(g); break;
    case 0x0C: swi_cpu_fast_set(g); break;
    case 0x0E: swi_affine_set(g); break;
    default: break;
    }
    /* clear halt if we just returned from a wait that should continue */
    /* normal return: PC was already incremented by arm_exec */
}
```

```
# GBA Emulator

[![CI](https://github.com/amyanger/gba-emulator/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/amyanger/gba-emulator/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![Release](https://github.com/amyanger/gba-emulator/actions/workflows/release.yml/badge.svg?event=push)](https://github.com/amyanger/gba-emulator/actions/workflows/release.yml)
[![Latest release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/amyanger/gba-emulator?label=release)](https://github.com/amyanger/gba-emulator/releases/latest)

A Game Boy Advance emulator written from scratch in C, featuring **Hardware X-Ray Mode**: a real-time view of what the GBA hardware is actually doing while a game runs.

No other GBA emulator offers this. Every emulator is a black box. This one lets you see inside.

Built around an ARM7TDMI CPU interpreter, scanline-based PPU, and an SDL2 frontend. No external libraries beyond SDL2. Pokemon Emerald is fully playable end-to-end.

**Jump to:** [Download](#download) · [Features](#features) · [Screenshots](#screenshots) · [Quick start](#quick-start) · [Building](#building-from-source) · [Documentation](#documentation)
```

```
static void gba_pc_hook_trampoline(void* ctx) {
    GBA* gba = (GBA*)ctx;
    gba->pc_hook(gba, gba->pc_hook_ctx);
}

void gba_set_pc_hook(GBA* gba, uint32_t addr, GbaPcHook fn, void* ctx) {
    gba->pc_hook = fn;
    gba->pc_hook_ctx = fn ? ctx : NULL;
    gba->cpu.pc_hook = fn ? gba_pc_hook_trampoline : NULL;
    gba->cpu.pc_hook_ctx = fn ? gba : NULL;
    gba->cpu.pc_hook_addr = fn ? addr : 0;
}

void gba_set_link_peer(GBA* gba, LinkPeer* peer) {
    gba->sio.peer = peer;
```

```
}

void gba_write8(GBA *g, uint32_t addr, uint8_t v) {
    switch (addr >> 24) {
    case 0x02: g->ewram[addr & 0x3FFFF] = v; return;
    case 0x03: g->iwram[addr & 0x7FFF] = v; return;
    case 0x04: {
                 /* HALTCNT (0x04000301). The BIOS Halt/IntrWait loops write
                    it to suspend the CPU until an IRQ arrives; without it the
                    BIOS never reaches the cartridge. Mask off the whole
                    region nibble, not 0x0FFFFFFF, or the compare never hits. */
                 if ((addr & 0x00FFFFFF) == 0x000301) {
                     g->io[0x301] = v;
                     g->cst.halt = true;
                     if (v == 0x80) g->cst.stopped = true;
                     return;
                 }
                 uint16_t cur = io_read16(g, addr & ~1u);
                 if (addr & 1) cur = (uint16_t)((cur & 0x00FF) | (v << 8));
                 else cur = (uint16_t)((cur & 0xFF00) | v);
                 io_write16(g, addr & ~1u, cur); return; }
    case 0x05: g->pal[addr & 0x3FF] = v; return;
    case 0x06: g->vram[addr & 0x17FFF] = v; return;
    case 0x07: g->oam[addr & 0x3FF] = v; return;
    case 0x0D: return;
    case 0x0E: g->save_mem[addr & 0x1FFFF] = v; return;
    default: return;
    }
}
```

```
static FILE* g_baio = NULL;
static int   g_baio_init = 0;

static void ba_iotrace(uint32_t addr, uint32_t val, int size) {
    if (!g_baio_init) { g_baio_init = 1; const char* p = getenv("BA_IOTRACE"); if (p) g_baio = fopen(p, "w"); }

        fprintf(g_baio, "%08X %08X %d\n", addr, val, size); g_baio_n++;
    }
```
```
}

void interrupt_request(InterruptController* ic, uint16_t irq_bit) {
    interrupt_request_late(ic, irq_bit, 0);

void interrupt_request_if_enabled(InterruptController* ic, PPU* ppu, uint16_t irq_bit,
                                  int32_t late) {
    // Check DISPSTAT enable bits for PPU-related IRQs
    if (irq_bit == IRQ_VBLANK && !(ppu->dispstat & (1 << 3))) return;
    if (irq_bit == IRQ_HBLANK && !(ppu->dispstat & (1 << 4))) return;
    if (irq_bit == IRQ_VCOUNT && !(ppu->dispstat & (1 << 5))) return;

    interrupt_request_late(ic, irq_bit, late);
}

/* mGBA's GBATestIRQ: if IE & IF, schedule a dispatch check 'delay'
 * cycles out unless one is already pending (the earliest one wins). */
void interrupt_test(InterruptController* ic, int32_t delay) {
    if ((ic->ie & ic->irf) && !ic->check_pending) {
        ic->check_pending = true;
        ic->check_delay = delay;
    }
}

void interrupt_elapse(InterruptController* ic, int32_t cycles) {
    if (ic->check_pending) {
        ic->check_delay -= cycles;
    }
}

/* Consume the pending check if its time has come. */
bool interrupt_check_due(InterruptController* ic) {
    if (!ic->check_pending || ic->check_delay > 0) return false;
    ic->check_pending = false;
    return true;
}
```

```
static void swi_div32(GBA *g) {
    int32_t a = (int32_t)g->cpu.r[0];
    int32_t b = (int32_t)g->cpu.r[1];
    if (b == 0) { g->cpu.r[0] = a; g->cpu.r[1] = a; g->cpu.r[3] = 0; return; }
```

```
/* Minimal driver for the reference core: run N frames headless and dump a
   PC trace so it can be diffed against our emulator. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include "gba.h"

static FILE *g_pc;
static long  g_pcn;

static void pc_hook(const struct GBA *gba, void *ctx) {
    (void)ctx;
    if (!g_pc) return;
    uint32_t pc = gba->cpu.regs[15] - 4u;   /* executing PC */
    if (g_pcn < 4000000) { fprintf(g_pc, "%08X\n", pc); g_pcn++; }
}

int main(int argc, char **argv) {
    if (argc < 3) { fprintf(stderr, "usage: %s rom bios [frames] [log_from_frame]\n", argv[0]); return 2; }
    int frames = argc > 3 ? atoi(argv[3]) : 400;
    int log_from = argc > 4 ? atoi(argv[4]) : 0;

    GBA *g = calloc(1, sizeof(GBA));
    gba_init(g);
    if (!gba_load_bios(g, argv[2])) { fprintf(stderr, "bios load failed\n"); return 1; }
    if (!gba_load_rom(g, argv[1], NULL)) { fprintf(stderr, "rom load failed\n"); return 1; }

    g_pc = fopen("/workspace/h/ref_pc.txt", "w");

    for (int i = 0; i < frames; i++) {
        if (i == log_from) {
            gba_set_pc_hook(g, 0x082E7DCC, pc_hook, NULL);
        }
        gba_run_frame(g);
    }
    fclose(g_pc);
    printf("done frames=%d pc_hook_hits=%ld DISPCNT=%04X\n",
           frames, g_pcn, g->ppu.dispcnt);
    return 0;
}
```

```
void gba_swi(GBA *g, uint32_t comment) {
    uint32_t swi_num = comment & 0xFF;

    /* Advance the program counter past the SWI instruction before running
       the handler. Handlers such as Halt/IntrWait set cst.halt, which the
       frame loop then uses to sleep the CPU until the next interrupt. */
    if (thumb_mode_p(g)) g->cpu.r[15] += 2;
    else                 g->cpu.r[15] += 4;

    switch (swi_num) {
    case 0x00: swi_soft_reset(g); break;
    case 0x01: swi_register_ram_reset(g); break;
    case 0x02: swi_halt(g); break;
    case 0x03: swi_stop(g); break;
    case 0x04: swi_intr_wait(g); break;
    case 0x05: swi_vblank_intr_wait(g); break;
    case 0x06: swi_div32(g); break;
    case 0x07: swi_div_arm(g); break;
    case 0x08: swi_sqrt(g); break;
    case 0x0B: swi_cpu_set(g); break;
    case 0x0C: swi_cpu_fast_set(g); break;
    case 0x0E: swi_affine_set(g); break;
    default: break;
    }
    /* clear halt if we just returned from a wait that should continue */
    /* normal return: PC was already incremented by arm_exec */
}
```

```
static void swi_register_ram_reset(GBA *g) {
    /* SWI 0x01: clear the memory regions selected by r0 and force the display
       into forced blank. Mirrors the hardware behaviour that games rely on to
       reinitialise their own shadow of the video registers. */
    uint32_t flags = g->cpu.r[0];

    g->ppu.dispcnt = 0x0080;
    g->io[0x00] = 0x80; g->io[0x01] = 0x00;

    if (flags & 0x01) memset(g->ewram, 0, EWRAM_SIZE);
    if (flags & 0x02) memset(g->iwram, 0, IWRAM_SIZE - 0x200);
    if (flags & 0x04) memset(g->pal, 0, PAL_SIZE);
    if (flags & 0x08) memset(g->vram, 0, VRAM_SIZE);
    if (flags & 0x10) memset(g->oam, 0, OAM_SIZE);

    if (flags & 0x20) {
        /* SIO registers 0x120-0x12F */
        for (int off = 0x120; off < 0x130; off += 2) { g->io[off] = 0; g->io[off+1] = 0; }
    }
    if (flags & 0x40) {
        /* Sound registers 0x060-0x0AF, SOUNDBIAS keeps its 0x200 default */
        memset(g->io + 0x60, 0, 0xB0 - 0x60);
        g->io[0x88] = 0x00; g->io[0x89] = 0x02;
    }
    if (flags & 0x80) {
        memset(g->io + 0x00, 0, 0x60);
        g->io[0x00] = 0x80; g->io[0x01] = 0x00;   /* DISPCNT: forced blank */
        memset(g->io + 0xB0, 0, 0xE0 - 0xB0);     /* DMA */
        memset(g->io + 0x100, 0, 0x10);           /* timers */
        memset(g->io + 0x130, 0, 4);              /* keypad */
        g->ie = 0;
        g->if_reg = 0xFFFF;
        g->io[0x204] = 0; g->io[0x205] = 0;       /* WAITCNT */
        g->ime = false;
    }
}
```

```
static void _Div(struct GBA* gba, int32_t num, int32_t denom) {
        struct ARMCore* cpu = gba->cpu;
        if (denom == 0) {
                if (num == 0 || num == -1 || num == 1) {
                        mLOG(GBA_BIOS, GAME_ERROR, "Attempting to divide %i by zero!", num);
                } else {
                        mLOG(GBA_BIOS, FATAL, "Attempting to divide %i by zero!", num);
                }
                // If abs(num) > 1, this should hang, but that would be painful to
                // emulate in HLE, and no game will get into a state under normal
                // operation where it hangs...
                cpu->gprs[0] = (num < 0) ? -1 : 1;
                cpu->gprs[1] = num;
                cpu->gprs[3] = 1;
        } else if (denom == -1 && num == INT32_MIN) {
                mLOG(GBA_BIOS, GAME_ERROR, "Attempting to divide INT_MIN by -1!");
                cpu->gprs[0] = INT32_MIN;
                cpu->gprs[1] = 0;
                cpu->gprs[3] = INT32_MIN;
        } else {
                div_t result = div(num, denom);
                cpu->gprs[0] = result.quot;
                cpu->gprs[1] = result.rem;
                cpu->gprs[3] = abs(result.quot);
        }
        int loops = clz32(denom) - clz32(num);
        if (loops < 1) {
                loops = 1;
        }
        gba->biosStall = 4 /* prologue */ + 13 * loops + 7 /* epilogue */;
}
```

```
 * bios.c - GBA BIOS SWI handlers.
 * Clean-room implementation of the classic GBA BIOS calls used to boot games.

#include "gba.h"
#include "mem.h"
#include <string.h>

static inline bool thumb_mode_p(GBA *g) { return (g->cpu.cpsr & CPSR_T) != 0; }

static void swi_soft_reset(GBA *g) {
    /* SWI 0x00: restart from the BIOS entry (0x00000000) after clearing the
       BIOS scratch area. Games use it as a full console reset; unlike
       RegisterRamReset it does not touch the I/O registers or the CPU mode. */
    memset(g->iwram + 0x7E00, 0, 0x200);
    g->cpu.r[13] = 0x03007F00;
    g->cpu.cpsr = 0x0000001F;            /* system mode, ARM, IRQ enabled */
    g->cpu.r[15] = 0x00000000;
}
```

```
static void enter_exception(GBA *g, uint32_t mode, uint32_t lr_val, uint32_t pc_addr) {
    uint32_t old = get_cpsr(g);
    g->cpu.spsr[bank_of(mode)] = old;               /* SPSR_<mode> = CPSR */

    g->cpu.r[14] = lr_val;                          /* LR_<mode> */
    set_pc(g, pc_addr);
}
```

```
/* Minimal driver for the reference core: run N frames headless and dump a
   PC trace so it can be diffed against our emulator. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include "gba.h"

static FILE *g_pc;
static long  g_pcn;

static void pc_hook(const struct GBA *gba, void *ctx) {
    (void)ctx;
    if (!g_pc) return;
    uint32_t pc = gba->cpu.regs[15] - 4u;   /* executing PC */
    if (g_pcn < 4000000) { fprintf(g_pc, "%08X\n", pc); g_pcn++; }
}

int main(int argc, char **argv) {
    if (argc < 3) { fprintf(stderr, "usage: %s rom bios [frames] [log_from_frame]\n", argv[0]); return 2; }
    int frames = argc > 3 ? atoi(argv[3]) : 400;
    int log_from = argc > 4 ? atoi(argv[4]) : 0;

    GBA *g = calloc(1, sizeof(GBA));
    gba_init(g);
    if (!gba_load_bios(g, argv[2])) { fprintf(stderr, "bios load failed\n"); return 1; }
    if (!gba_load_rom(g, argv[1], NULL)) { fprintf(stderr, "rom load failed\n"); return 1; }

    g_pc = fopen("/workspace/h/ref_pc.txt", "w");

    for (int i = 0; i < frames; i++) {
        if (i == log_from) {
            gba_set_pc_hook(g, 0x082E7DCC, pc_hook, NULL);
        }
        gba_run_frame(g);
    }
    fclose(g_pc);
    printf("done frames=%d pc_hook_hits=%ld DISPCNT=%04X\n",
           frames, g_pcn, g->ppu.dispcnt);
    return 0;
}
```

```
/* Per-frame DISPCNT trace from the reference core, for side-by-side diffing. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include "gba.h"
int main(int argc, char **argv) {
    int frames = argc > 3 ? atoi(argv[3]) : 600;
    GBA *g = calloc(1, sizeof(GBA));
    gba_init(g);
    gba_load_bios(g, argv[2]);
    gba_load_rom(g, argv[1], NULL);
    uint16_t prev = 0xFFFF;
    for (int i = 0; i < frames; i++) {
        gba_run_frame(g);
        if (g->ppu.dispcnt != prev) {
            printf("f%-5d DISPCNT %04X -> %04X  pc=%08X\n", i, prev, g->ppu.dispcnt, g->cpu.regs[15]);
            prev = g->ppu.dispcnt;
        }
    }
    printf("END f=%d DISPCNT=%04X pc=%08X\n", frames, g->ppu.dispcnt, g->cpu.regs[15]);
    return 0;
}
```

```
#ifndef INTERRUPT_H
#define INTERRUPT_H

#include "common.h"

// Forward declaration
typedef struct PPU PPU;

/* Cycles from an IRQ being raised to the CPU taking it (mGBA's
 * GBA_IRQ_DELAY). IF is visible at once; dispatch and HALT wake wait. */
#define IRQ_DISPATCH_DELAY 7

struct InterruptController {
    bool ime;       // Interrupt Master Enable
    uint16_t ie;    // Interrupt Enable
    uint16_t irf;   // Interrupt Request Flags

    // Delayed dispatch check (mGBA's irqEvent). check_delay counts down
    // from the start of the CPU instruction in flight (or from the
    // current boundary between instructions); cpu_run takes the check at
    // the first boundary where it is <= 0. Not saved: a loaded state
    // re-arms it with no delay.
    bool check_pending;
    int32_t check_delay;
};
```

```
/* Log writes to DISPCNT (0x04000000) and DISPSTAT (0x04000004) with PC. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include "gba.h"
#include "mem.h"
#include "arm.h"

static FILE *out;
static int cur_frame;

int main(int argc, char **argv) {
    int frames = argc > 3 ? atoi(argv[3]) : 400;
    GBA *g = calloc(1, sizeof(GBA));
    gba_init(g);
    gba_load_bios(g, argv[2]);
    gba_load_rom(g, argv[1]);
    g->bios_fastboot = false;
    gba_reset(g);
    out = fopen("/workspace/h/iolog.txt", "w");
    for (cur_frame = 0; cur_frame < frames; cur_frame++) {
        for (int line = 0; line < 228; line++) {
            g->ppu.vcount = (uint16_t)line;
            uint16_t st = (uint16_t)(g->ppu.dispstat & 0xFFF8);
            if (line >= 160) st |= 0x0001;
            if (line < 160)  st |= 0x0002;
            if (line == ((g->ppu.dispstat >> 8) & 0xFF)) st |= 0x0004;
            g->ppu.dispstat = st;
            if (line == 160) {
                if (g->ppu.dispstat & 0x0008) g->if_reg |= IF_VBLANK;
                ppu_render_frame(g); g->frame_count++;
                if (g->cst.halt) g->cst.halt = false;
                dma_trigger(g, 1);
            }
            if (g->ppu.dispstat & 0x0010) g->if_reg |= IF_HBLANK;
            if (line < 160) dma_trigger(g, 2);
```

```
bool trace_init(const char* path, uint32_t pc_from, uint32_t pc_to, uint32_t max_frames) {
    if (!path) return false;
    if (s_trace.fp) trace_shutdown();

}
```

```
void gba_run_cycles(GBA* gba, int cycles) {
    int32_t remaining = cycles - gba->cycle_carry;

    while (remaining > 0) {
        // End the slice where a timer IRQ fires so the CPU sees it on time.
        int32_t slice = timer_cycles_until_irq(gba->timers);
        if (slice > remaining) slice = remaining;
        // Timer writes end a slice early (bus.end_slice) so this is
        // re-planned. Always run at least one cycle so a stale prediction
        // (e.g. a loaded state's prescaler count) can't loop forever.
        if (slice < 1) slice = 1;

        cpu_run(&gba->cpu, slice);
        int32_t ran = gba->cpu.cycles_executed;

        // Timer writes mid-slice already synced part of it; tick the rest.
        int32_t unsynced = ran - gba->bus.timer_synced_cycles;
        if (unsynced > 0) {
            timer_tick(gba->timers, unsynced, &gba->interrupts, &gba->apu);
        }
        gba->bus.timer_synced_cycles = 0;
        apu_tick(&gba->apu, ran);
        sio_tick(&gba->sio, ran);
        // Timers are now synced; clear the CPU's slice progress so timer
        // reads don't project these cycles a second time.
        gba->cpu.cycles_executed = 0;

        remaining -= ran;
    }

    gba->cycle_carry = -remaining;
}
```

```
static void swi_register_ram_reset(GBA *g) {
    /* SWI 0x01: clear the memory regions selected by r0 and force the display
       into forced blank. Mirrors the hardware behaviour that games rely on to
       reinitialise their own shadow of the video registers. */
    uint32_t flags = g->cpu.r[0];

    g->ppu.dispcnt = 0x0080;
    g->io[0x00] = 0x80; g->io[0x01] = 0x00;

    if (flags & 0x01) memset(g->ewram, 0, EWRAM_SIZE);
    if (flags & 0x02) memset(g->iwram, 0, IWRAM_SIZE - 0x200);
    if (flags & 0x04) memset(g->pal, 0, PAL_SIZE);
    if (flags & 0x08) memset(g->vram, 0, VRAM_SIZE);
    if (flags & 0x10) memset(g->oam, 0, OAM_SIZE);

    if (flags & 0x20) {
        /* SIO registers 0x120-0x12F */
        for (int off = 0x120; off < 0x130; off += 2) { g->io[off] = 0; g->io[off+1] = 0; }
    }
    if (flags & 0x40) {
        /* Sound registers 0x060-0x0AF, SOUNDBIAS keeps its 0x200 default */
        memset(g->io + 0x60, 0, 0xB0 - 0x60);
        g->io[0x88] = 0x00; g->io[0x89] = 0x02;
    }
    if (flags & 0x80) {
        memset(g->io + 0x00, 0, 0x60);
        g->io[0x00] = 0x80; g->io[0x01] = 0x00;   /* DISPCNT: forced blank */
```

```
    *reg = hi ? (uint16_t)((*reg & 0x00FF) | ((uint16_t)val << 8))
              : (uint16_t)((*reg & 0xFF00) | val);
}
```

```
void gba_update_keypad(GBA *g, uint16_t keys) {
    g->key_input = (uint16_t)(~keys) & 0x3FF;  /* 0 = pressed */
    io_trigger_keypad(g, 0);
```

```
=== body ===
void arm_execute(GBA *g, uint32_t max_cycles) {
    uint32_t start = g->cycle;
    while (g->cycle - start < max_cycles) {
        /* A halted CPU wakes as soon as an *enabled* interrupt is requested
           (IE & IF), regardless of IME or the CPSR I bit; IME only gates the
           exception vectoring below. Missing this stalls the CPU until the
           next VBlank and desynchronises code that polls VCOUNT. */
        if (g->cst.halt && (g->if_reg & g->ie & 0x3FFF)) g->cst.halt = false;

        /* IRQ exception has priority over halt. IF is NOT acknowledged here:
         * the GBA leaves the flag set so the handler can read IE&IF to find
         * the source; the BIOS/handler clears it by writing 1 to IF. */
        if (g->ime && (g->if_reg & g->ie & 0x3FFF) && !(g->cpu.cpsr & CPSR_I)) {
            g->cst.halt = false;   /* an enabled IRQ wakes the CPU from Halt */
            enter_exception(g, 0x12, g->cpu.r[15] + (thumb_mode(g) ? 2 : 4), 0x18);
            continue;
        }
        if (g->cst.halt) {
            /* CPU asleep: just burn cycles until the scanline/frame budget ends */
            g->cycle = start + max_cycles;
            break;
        }
        if (thumb_mode(g)) thumb_exec(g);
        else arm_exec(g);
    }
}
```

```
static void swi_cpu_fast_set(GBA *g) {
    uint32_t src = g->cpu.r[0];
    uint32_t dst = g->cpu.r[1];
    uint32_t ctl = g->cpu.r[2];
    uint32_t count = ctl & 0x1FFFFF;
    bool fixed = ctl & 0x01000000;
    bool is32 = ctl & 0x04000000;
    if (is32) {
        for (uint32_t i = 0; i < count; i++) {
            uint32_t v = gba_read32(g, src);
            gba_write32(g, dst, v);
            if (!fixed) src += 4;
            dst += 4;
        }
    } else {
        for (uint32_t i = 0; i < count; i++) {
```

```
static void swi_soft_reset(GBA *g) {
    /* SWI 0x00: restart from the BIOS entry (0x00000000) or the EWRAM entry
       depending on the boot flag at 0x03007FFA. Mirrors the real BIOS: the
       BIOS scratch area is cleared, the SYS/IRQ/SVC stack pointers are
       restored, and the CPU resumes in SYS mode with IRQs enabled. */
    uint32_t boot_target = (g->iwram[0x7FFA] != 0) ? 0x02000000 : 0x08000000;

    memset(g->iwram + 0x7E00, 0, 0x200);
    g->cpu.bank[BANK_IRQ][5] = 0x03007FA0;
    g->cpu.bank[BANK_SVC][5] = 0x03007FE0;
    g->cpu.bank[0][5] = 0x03007F00;
    g->cpu.r[13] = 0x03007F00;
    g->cpu.cpsr = 0x0000001F;            /* system mode, ARM, IRQ enabled */
    g->cpu.r[15] = boot_target;
}
```

```
static void swi_intr_wait(GBA *g) {
    /* SWI 0x04: wait for any of the IRQs in r0; r1=1 discards old flags.
       We let the frame loop keep running and only halt the CPU here. */
    g->cst.halt = true;
}
=== vblank ===
static void swi_vblank_intr_wait(GBA *g) {
    /* SWI 0x05: VBlankIntrWait. Equivalent to IntrWait(1,1).
       Halt until the VBlank IRQ condition is met; the frame loop clears
       halt as soon as IF_VBLANK is raised. */
    g->cst.halt = true;
}
=== halt ===
static void swi_halt(GBA *g) {
    g->cst.halt = true;
}
```

```
static void swi_register_ram_reset(GBA *g) {
    /* SWI 0x01: clear the memory regions selected by r0 and force the display
       into forced blank. Mirrors the hardware behaviour that games rely on to
       reinitialise their own shadow of the video registers. */
    uint32_t flags = g->cpu.r[0];

    g->ppu.dispcnt = 0x0080;
    g->io[0x00] = 0x80; g->io[0x01] = 0x00;

    if (flags & 0x01) memset(g->ewram, 0, EWRAM_SIZE);
    if (flags & 0x02) memset(g->iwram, 0, IWRAM_SIZE - 0x200);
    if (flags & 0x04) memset(g->pal, 0, PAL_SIZE);
    if (flags & 0x08) memset(g->vram, 0, VRAM_SIZE);
    if (flags & 0x10) memset(g->oam, 0, OAM_SIZE);

    if (flags & 0x20) {
        /* SIO registers 0x120-0x12F */
        for (int off = 0x120; off < 0x130; off += 2) { g->io[off] = 0; g->io[off+1] = 0; }
    }
    if (flags & 0x40) {
        /* Sound registers 0x060-0x0AF, SOUNDBIAS keeps its 0x200 default */
        memset(g->io + 0x60, 0, 0xB0 - 0x60);
        g->io[0x88] = 0x00; g->io[0x89] = 0x02;
    }
    if (flags & 0x80) {
        memset(g->io + 0x00, 0, 0x60);
        g->io[0x00] = 0x80; g->io[0x01] = 0x00;   /* DISPCNT: forced blank */
```

```
/* Reference PC trace writer: dumps every executed PC for N frames. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include "gba.h"

extern FILE* g_pclog;
extern long g_pclog_n;

int main(int argc, char **argv) {
    int frames = argc > 3 ? atoi(argv[3]) : 300;
    GBA *g = calloc(1, sizeof(GBA));
    gba_init(g);
    gba_load_bios(g, argv[2]);
    gba_load_rom(g, argv[1], NULL);
    g_pclog = fopen("/workspace/h/refpc.txt", "w");
    for (int i = 0; i < frames; i++) gba_run_frame(g);
    fclose(g_pclog);
    printf("done frames=%d instr=%ld\n", frames, g_pclog_n);
    return 0;
}
```

```
void gba_run_cycles(GBA* gba, int cycles) {
    int32_t remaining = cycles - gba->cycle_carry;

    while (remaining > 0) {
        // End the slice where a timer IRQ fires so the CPU sees it on time.
        int32_t slice = timer_cycles_until_irq(gba->timers);
        if (slice > remaining) slice = remaining;
        // Timer writes end a slice early (bus.end_slice) so this is
        // re-planned. Always run at least one cycle so a stale prediction
        // (e.g. a loaded state's prescaler count) can't loop forever.
        if (slice < 1) slice = 1;

        cpu_run(&gba->cpu, slice);
        int32_t ran = gba->cpu.cycles_executed;

        // Timer writes mid-slice already synced part of it; tick the rest.
        int32_t unsynced = ran - gba->bus.timer_synced_cycles;
        if (unsynced > 0) {
            timer_tick(gba->timers, unsynced, &gba->interrupts, &gba->apu);
        }
        gba->bus.timer_synced_cycles = 0;
        apu_tick(&gba->apu, ran);
        sio_tick(&gba->sio, ran);
        // Timers are now synced; clear the CPU's slice progress so timer
        // reads don't project these cycles a second time.
        gba->cpu.cycles_executed = 0;

        remaining -= ran;
    }

    gba->cycle_carry = -remaining;
}
```

```
void gba_write8(GBA *g, uint32_t addr, uint8_t v) {
    switch (addr >> 24) {
    case 0x02: g->ewram[addr & 0x3FFFF] = v; return;
    case 0x03: g->iwram[addr & 0x7FFF] = v; return;
    case 0x04: {
                 /* HALTCNT (0x04000301). The BIOS Halt/IntrWait loops write
                    it to suspend the CPU until an IRQ arrives; without it the
                    BIOS never reaches the cartridge. Mask off the whole
                    region nibble, not 0x0FFFFFFF, or the compare never hits. */
                 if ((addr & 0x00FFFFFF) == 0x000301) {
                     g->io[0x301] = v;
                     g->cst.halt = true;
                     if (v == 0x80) g->cst.stopped = true;
                     return;
                 }
                 uint16_t cur = io_read16(g, addr & ~1u);
                 if (addr & 1) cur = (uint16_t)((cur & 0x00FF) | (v << 8));
                 else cur = (uint16_t)((cur & 0xFF00) | v);
                 io_write16(g, addr & ~1u, cur); return; }
    case 0x05: g->pal[addr & 0x3FF] = v; return;
    case 0x06: g->vram[addr & 0x17FFF] = v; return;
    case 0x07: g->oam[addr & 0x3FF] = v; return;
    case 0x0D: return;
    case 0x0E: g->save_mem[addr & 0x1FFFF] = v; return;
    default: return;
    }
}
```

```
#define MACRONIX_DEVICE_128K  0x09

void flash_init(FlashChip* flash, bool is_128k) {
    memset(flash->data, 0xFF, sizeof(flash->data));
    flash->state = FLASH_READY;
    flash->bank = 0;

    if (is_128k) {
        flash->manufacturer = MACRONIX_MANUFACTURER;
        flash->device = MACRONIX_DEVICE_128K;
    } else {
        flash->manufacturer = SANYO_MANUFACTURER;
        flash->device = SANYO_DEVICE_64K;
    }
}

uint8_t flash_read(FlashChip* flash, uint32_t addr) {
    addr &= 0xFFFF;

    if (flash->state == FLASH_AUTOSELECT) {
        if (addr == 0x0000) return flash->manufacturer;
        if (addr == 0x0001) return flash->device;
        return 0;
    }

    return flash->data[flash->bank * 0x10000 + addr];
}
```

```
def load(p): return [l.strip() for l in open(p)]
def collapse(pcs):
    """Remove repeated loop bodies: detect cycles of length 1..4 and keep one instance."""
    out=[]
    i=0; n=len(pcs)
    while i<n:
        matched=False
        for L in (1,2,3,4):
            if i+2*L<=n and pcs[i:i+L]==pcs[i+L:i+2*L]:
                # find how many repeats
                reps=1
                while i+(reps+1)*L<=n and pcs[i:i+L]==pcs[i+reps*L:i+(reps+1)*L]:
                    reps+=1
                out.extend(pcs[i:i+L])
                i+=reps*L
                matched=True
                break
        if not matched:
            out.append(pcs[i]); i+=1
    return out
```

```
            if (line < 160)  st |= 0x0002;
```

```
static void enter_exception(GBA *g, uint32_t mode, uint32_t lr_val, uint32_t pc_addr) {
    uint32_t old = get_cpsr(g);
    g->cpu.spsr[bank_of(mode)] = old;               /* SPSR_<mode> = CPSR */
    /* Vectors run in ARM state; force IRQ-disable and clear the Thumb bit. */
    change_mode(g, (old & ~0x3Fu) | mode | CPSR_I);
    g->cpu.r[14] = lr_val;                          /* LR_<mode> */
    set_pc(g, pc_addr);
}
```

```
    Ppu *p = &g->ppu;
    uint16_t dispcnt = p->dispcnt;
    int bg_mode = dispcnt & 0x7;
    bool obj_enabled = dispcnt & 0x1000;

    uint16_t backdrop = read_pal(g, 0);
```

```
/* Reference per-frame IO state dump for the frames around the reset. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include "gba.h"

static FILE *out;
static int frame;

static void obs(const struct GBA *gba, void *ctx) {
    (void)ctx;
    if (frame >= 260)
        fprintf(out, "f%-4d DISPCNT=%04X DISPSTAT=%04X IE=%04X IF=%04X IME=%d PC=%08X\n",
                frame, gba->ppu.dispcnt, gba->ppu.dispstat, gba->interrupts.ie,
                gba->interrupts.irf, gba->interrupts.ime, gba->cpu.regs[15] - 4u);
    frame++;
}

int main(int argc, char **argv) {
    int frames = argc > 3 ? atoi(argv[3]) : 300;
    GBA *g = calloc(1, sizeof(GBA));
    gba_init(g);
    gba_load_bios(g, argv[2]);
    gba_load_rom(g, argv[1], NULL);
    out = fopen("/workspace/h/refstate.txt", "w");
    gba_set_vblank_observer(g, obs, NULL);
    for (int i = 0; i < frames; i++) gba_run_frame(g);
    fclose(out);
    printf("done\n");
    return 0;
}
```

```
/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
/* public loop                                                         */
/* ------------------------------------------------------------------ */
void arm_execute(GBA *g, uint32_t max_cycles) {
    uint32_t start = g->cycle;
    while (g->cycle - start < max_cycles) {
        /* A halted CPU wakes as soon as an *enabled* interrupt is requested
           (IE & IF), regardless of IME or the CPSR I bit; IME only gates the
           exception vectoring below. Missing this stalls the CPU until the
           next VBlank and desynchronises code that polls VCOUNT. */
        if (g->cst.halt && (g->if_reg & g->ie & 0x3FFF)) g->cst.halt = false;

        /* IRQ exception has priority over halt. IF is NOT acknowledged here:
         * the GBA leaves the flag set so the handler can read IE&IF to find
         * the source; the BIOS/handler clears it by writing 1 to IF. */
        if (g->ime && (g->if_reg & g->ie & 0x3FFF) && !(g->cpu.cpsr & CPSR_I)) {
            g->cst.halt = false;   /* an enabled IRQ wakes the CPU from Halt */
            enter_exception(g, 0x12, g->cpu.r[15] + (thumb_mode(g) ? 2 : 4), 0x18);
            continue;
        }
        if (g->cst.halt) {
            /* CPU asleep: just burn cycles until the scanline/frame budget ends */
            g->cycle = start + max_cycles;
            break;
        }
        if (thumb_mode(g)) thumb_exec(g);
        else arm_exec(g);
    }
}
```

```
uint32_t gba_read32(GBA *g, uint32_t addr) {
    switch (addr >> 24) {
    case 0x00: return rd32_al(g->bios + (addr & 0x3FFC));
    case 0x02: return rd32_al(g->ewram + (addr & 0x3FFFC));
    case 0x03: return rd32_al(g->iwram + (addr & 0x7FFC));
    case 0x04: return io_read16(g, addr) | ((uint32_t)io_read16(g, addr + 2) << 16);
    case 0x05: return rd32_al(g->pal + (addr & 0x3FC));
    case 0x06: return rd32_al(g->vram + (addr & 0x17FFC));
    case 0x07: return rd32_al(g->oam + (addr & 0x3FC));
    case 0x08: case 0x09: case 0x0A: case 0x0B: case 0x0C: case 0x0D: {
        if (eeprom_addr_in_range(g, addr)) return 0;  /* EEPROM reads are bit-serial via DMA */
        uint32_t off = (addr - 0x08000000) & (g->rom_mask & ~3u);
        return off < g->rom_size ? rd32_al(g->rom + off) : 0;
    }
    case 0x0E: {
        if (flash_in_use(g)) return rd32_al(g->save_mem + (g->flash.bank * 0x10000) + (addr & 0xFFFC));
        return rd32_al(g->save_mem + (addr & 0x1FFFC));
    }
    default: return 0;
    }
}
```

```
/* Reference PC trace writer: dumps every executed PC for N frames. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include "gba.h"

extern FILE* g_pclog;
extern long g_pclog_n;

int main(int argc, char **argv) {
    int frames = argc > 3 ? atoi(argv[3]) : 300;
    GBA *g = calloc(1, sizeof(GBA));
    gba_init(g);
    gba_load_bios(g, argv[2]);
    gba_load_rom(g, argv[1], NULL);
    g_pclog = fopen("/workspace/h/refpc.txt", "w");
    for (int i = 0; i < frames; i++) gba_run_frame(g);
    fclose(g_pclog);
    printf("done frames=%d instr=%ld\n", frames, g_pclog_n);
    return 0;
}
```

```
/* Dump the reference PPU framebuffer at a given frame for comparison. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include "gba.h"

int main(int argc, char **argv) {
    int frames = argc > 3 ? atoi(argv[3]) : 300;
    const char *outp = argc > 4 ? argv[4] : "/workspace/h/ref_fb.bin";
    GBA *g = calloc(1, sizeof(GBA));
    gba_init(g);
    gba_load_bios(g, argv[2]);
    gba_load_rom(g, argv[1], NULL);
    for (int i = 0; i < frames; i++) gba_run_frame(g);
    FILE *f = fopen(outp, "wb");
    fwrite(g->ppu.framebuffer, sizeof(uint16_t), 240 * 160, f);
    fclose(f);
    printf("dispcnt=%04X\n", g->ppu.dispcnt);
    return 0;
}
```

```
long g_vram_writes;
long g_vram_nonzero;
FILE *g_wlog;
void gba_write32(GBA *g, uint32_t addr, uint32_t v) {
    if (g_wlog && (addr >> 24) == 3 && (addr & 0x7FFF) == 0x22DC)
        fprintf(g_wlog, "w32 pc=%08X val=%08X\n", g->cpu.r[15], v);
    if ((addr >> 24) == 6) { g_vram_writes += 2; if (v) g_vram_nonzero += 2; }
    switch (addr >> 24) {
    case 0x02: wr32_al(g->ewram + (addr & 0x3FFFC), v); return;
    case 0x03: wr32_al(g->iwram + (addr & 0x7FFC), v); return;
    case 0x04: io_write16(g, addr, v & 0xFFFF); io_write16(g, addr + 2, v >> 16); return;
    case 0x05: wr32_al(g->pal + (addr & 0x3FC), v); return;
    case 0x06: wr32_al(g->vram + (addr & 0x17FFC), v); return;
    case 0x07: wr32_al(g->oam + (addr & 0x3FC), v); return;
    case 0x0D: return;   /* EEPROM writes go through DMA; the rest is ROM */
    case 0x0E:
        if (flash_in_use(g)) {
            flash_write(g, addr, (uint8_t)v);
            flash_write(g, addr + 1, (uint8_t)(v >> 8));
            flash_write(g, addr + 2, (uint8_t)(v >> 16));
            flash_write(g, addr + 3, (uint8_t)(v >> 24));
            return;
        }
        wr32_al(g->save_mem + (addr & 0x1FFFC), v); return;
    default: return;   /* ROM write-protected */
    }
}
```

```
bool gba_load_rom(GBA *g, const char *path) {
    FILE *f = fopen(path, "rb");
    if (!f) return false;
    fseek(f, 0, SEEK_END);
    long sz = ftell(f);
    fseek(f, 0, SEEK_SET);
    if (sz <= 0 || sz > ROM_MAX) { fclose(f); return false; }
    size_t got = fread(g->rom, 1, (size_t)sz, f);
    fclose(f);
    g->rom_size = (uint32_t)got;
    g->rom_mask = 0x1FFFFFF;
    if (g->rom_size <= 0x20000) g->rom_mask = 0x1FFFF;
    else if (g->rom_size <= 0x40000) g->rom_mask = 0x3FFFF;    /* 256K */
    else if (g->rom_size <= 0x80000) g->rom_mask = 0x7FFFF;    /* 512K */
    else if (g->rom_size <= 0x100000) g->rom_mask = 0xFFFFF;   /* 1M */
    else if (g->rom_size <= 0x200000) g->rom_mask = 0x1FFFFF;  /* 2M */
    else { g->rom_mask = 0x1FFFFFF; }
    /* title */
    memcpy(g->rom_title, g->rom + 0xA0, 12);
    g->rom_title[12] = 0;
    /* Save type from the marker strings Nintendo's save drivers leave in
       the ROM image (same heuristic as the reference implementations). */
    g->save_type = SAVE_NONE;
```

```
=== refpc.c ===
/* Reference PC trace writer: dumps every executed PC for N frames. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include "gba.h"

extern FILE* g_pclog;
extern long g_pclog_n;

int main(int argc, char **argv) {
    int frames = argc > 3 ? atoi(argv[3]) : 300;
    GBA *g = calloc(1, sizeof(GBA));
    gba_init(g);
    gba_load_bios(g, argv[2]);
    gba_load_rom(g, argv[1], NULL);
    g_pclog = fopen("/workspace/h/refpc.txt", "w");
    for (int i = 0; i < frames; i++) gba_run_frame(g);
    fclose(g_pclog);
    printf("done frames=%d instr=%ld\n", frames, g_pclog_n);
    return 0;
}
```

```
uint8_t gba_read8(GBA *g, uint32_t addr) {
    switch (addr >> 24) {
    case 0x00: return g->bios[addr & 0x3FFF];
    case 0x02: return g->ewram[addr & 0x3FFFF];
    case 0x03: return g->iwram[addr & 0x7FFF];
    case 0x04: { uint16_t v = io_read16(g, addr & ~1u); return (uint8_t)((addr & 1) ? (v >> 8) : v); }
    case 0x05: return g->pal[addr & 0x3FF];
    case 0x06: return g->vram[addr & 0x17FFF];
    case 0x07: return g->oam[addr & 0x3FF];
    case 0x08: case 0x09: case 0x0A: case 0x0B: case 0x0C: case 0x0D: {
        if (eeprom_addr_in_range(g, addr))
            return (addr & 1) ? 0 : eeprom_read_bit(g);   /* bit 0 of each halfword */
        uint32_t off = (addr - 0x08000000) & g->rom_mask;
        return off < g->rom_size ? g->rom[off] : 0;
    }
    case 0x0E: return flash_in_use(g) ? flash_read(g, addr) : g->save_mem[addr & 0x1FFFF];
    default: return 0;
    }
}
```

```
void gba_run_frame(GBA* gba) {
    gba->frame_complete = false;

    /* Sample the keypad IRQ condition at frame start, like mGBA's
     * GBAFrameStarted. Host key events arrive between frames. */
    bus_check_keypad_irq(&gba->bus);

    for (int line = 0; line < TOTAL_LINES; line++) {
        gba_run_scanline(gba);
    }

#ifdef ENABLE_REWIND
    /* Record snapshot at end-of-frame, after all scanlines (including VBlank)
     * have completed and the GBA struct represents a consistent state. */
    rewind_record_frame(&gba->rewind, gba);
#endif
}

void gba_set_vblank_observer(GBA* gba, GbaVblankObserver fn, void* ctx) {
    gba->vblank_observer = fn;
    gba->vblank_observer_ctx = fn ? ctx : NULL;
}

static void gba_pc_hook_trampoline(void* ctx) {
    GBA* gba = (GBA*)ctx;
    gba->pc_hook(gba, gba->pc_hook_ctx);
}
```

```
void bus_write16(Bus* bus, uint32_t addr, uint16_t val) {
    ba_iotrace(addr, val, 16);
    uint32_t lane = addr & 1;
    addr &= ~1u;
    bus_charge_access(bus, addr, 2, false);
    /* Palette, VRAM, and OAM need direct writes — the byte path has special
     * 8-bit behaviour (byte duplication / ignore) that would corrupt wider
     * writes if we decomposed into two byte writes. */
    switch (decode_region(addr)) {
    case 0x05: { /* Palette RAM — normal 16-bit write */
        uint32_t off = addr & (PALETTE_SIZE - 1);
        bus->palette_ram[off]     = (uint8_t)(val);
        bus->palette_ram[off + 1] = (uint8_t)(val >> 8);
        return;
    }
    case 0x06: { /* VRAM — normal 16-bit write */
        uint32_t off = vram_offset(addr);
        if (g_reftrace) fprintf(stderr, "vram w16 pc=%08X addr=%08X val=%04X
", g_baio_pc, addr, val);

        return;
```

```
void gba_swi(GBA *g, uint32_t comment) {
    uint32_t swi_num = comment & 0xFF;

    /* Advance the program counter past the SWI instruction before running
       the handler. Handlers such as Halt/IntrWait set cst.halt, which the
       frame loop then uses to sleep the CPU until the next interrupt. */
    if (thumb_mode_p(g)) g->cpu.r[15] += 2;
    else                 g->cpu.r[15] += 4;
```

```
/* SWI 0x14/0x15: RLE (run-length). Header 0x30. */
static void swi_rluncomp(GBA *g, bool vram) {
    uint32_t src = g->cpu.r[0];
    uint32_t dst = g->cpu.r[1];
    gba_read8(g, src++);                    /* header 0x30 */
    uint32_t left = swi_read_len(g, &src);
    while (left > 0) {
        uint8_t flags = gba_read8(g, src++);
        for (int i = 0; i < 8 && left > 0; i++) {
            if (flags & 0x80) {
                uint32_t count = (gba_read8(g, src++) & 0x7F) + 3;
                uint8_t v = gba_read8(g, src++);
                for (uint32_t k = 0; k < count && left > 0; k++) {
                    if (vram) gba_write16(g, dst, v); else gba_write8(g, dst, v);
                    dst++; left--;
                }
            } else {
                uint32_t count = (gba_read8(g, src++) & 0x7F) + 1;
                for (uint32_t k = 0; k < count && left > 0; k++) {
                    uint8_t v = gba_read8(g, src++);
                    if (vram) gba_write16(g, dst, v); else gba_write8(g, dst, v);
                    dst++; left--;
                }
            }
            flags <<= 1;
        }
    }
    g->cpu.r[0] = len;
}
```

```
/* cheats */
void gba_add_cheat(GBA *g, uint32_t addr, uint16_t value) {
    if (g->n_cheats < 100) {
        g->cheats[g->n_cheats].addr = addr & 0xFFFFFF;
        g->cheats[g->n_cheats].value = value;
        g->cheats[g->n_cheats].stored = 0;
        g->cheats[g->n_cheats].active = true;
        g->cheats[g->n_cheats].is_gameshark = false;
        g->n_cheats++;
    }
}
void gba_clear_cheats(GBA *g) { g->n_cheats = 0; }
void gba_apply_cheats(GBA *g) {
    for (int i = 0; i < g->n_cheats; i++) {
        if (!g->cheats[i].active) continue;
        uint32_t addr = g->cheats[i].addr;
        uint16_t v = g->cheats[i].value;
```

```
import struct, zlib, sys

def readfb(p):
    d = open(p, 'rb').read()
    return struct.unpack('<%dH' % (240 * 160), d)

def to_png(px, path):
    def rgb(c):
        r = (c & 31) * 255 // 31
        g = ((c >> 5) & 31) * 255 // 31
        b = ((c >> 10) & 31) * 255 // 31
        return bytes((r, g, b))
    raw = b''.join(b'\x00' + b''.join(rgb(px[y * 240 + x]) for x in range(240)) for y in range(160))
    def chunk(t, d):
        c = t + d
        return struct.pack('>I', len(d)) + c + struct.pack('>I', zlib.crc32(c) & 0xffffffff)
    png = (b'\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n' +
           chunk(b'IHDR', struct.pack('>IIBBBBB', 240, 160, 8, 2, 0, 0, 0)) +
           chunk(b'IDAT', zlib.compress(raw)) + chunk(b'IEND', b''))
    open(path, 'wb').write(png)
```

```
static void swi_affine_set(GBA *g) { (void)g; }

void gba_swi(GBA *g, uint32_t comment) {
    uint32_t swi_num = comment & 0xFF;

    /* Advance the program counter past the SWI instruction before running
       the handler. Handlers such as Halt/IntrWait set cst.halt, which the
       frame loop then uses to sleep the CPU until the next interrupt. */
    if (thumb_mode_p(g)) g->cpu.r[15] += 2;
    else                 g->cpu.r[15] += 4;

    switch (swi_num) {
    case 0x00: swi_soft_reset(g); break;
    case 0x01: swi_register_ram_reset(g); break;
    case 0x02: swi_halt(g); break;
    case 0x03: swi_stop(g); break;
    case 0x04: swi_intr_wait(g); break;
    case 0x05: swi_vblank_intr_wait(g); break;
    case 0x06: swi_div32(g); break;
    case 0x07: swi_div_arm(g); break;
    case 0x08: swi_sqrt(g); break;
    case 0x0B: swi_cpu_set(g); break;
    case 0x0C: swi_cpu_fast_set(g); break;
    case 0x0E: swi_affine_set(g); break;
    default: break;
    }
    /* clear halt if we just returned from a wait that should continue */
    /* normal return: PC was already incremented by arm_exec */
}
```

```
 * bios.c - GBA BIOS SWI handlers.
 * Clean-room implementation of the classic GBA BIOS calls used to boot games.

#include "mem.h"

static void swi_soft_reset(GBA *g) {
    /* SWI 0x00: restart from the BIOS entry (0x00000000) or the EWRAM entry
       depending on the boot flag at 0x03007FFA. Mirrors the real BIOS: the
       BIOS scratch area is cleared, the SYS/IRQ/SVC stack pointers are
       restored, and the CPU resumes in SYS mode with IRQs enabled. */
    uint32_t boot_target = (g->iwram[0x7FFA] != 0) ? 0x02000000 : 0x08000000;

    g->cpu.bank[BANK_SVC][5] = 0x03007FE0;
```

```
# Makefile.win32 - cross-compile the native Windows build (no SDL).
#
# The Windows build links directly to GDI / Direct3D 9 / waveOut (WinMM);
# SDL2 is intentionally not used. Build from Linux with a MinGW cross
# toolchain, or from Windows with MinGW-w64:
#
#   make -f Makefile.win32                     # x86_64, mingw64
#   make -f Makefile.win32 ARCH=i686           # i686, mingw32
#
# Variables:
#   CROSS  toolchain prefix (default: x86_64-w64-mingw32- / i686-w64-mingw32-)

ARCH ?= x86_64
ifeq ($(ARCH),i686)
  CROSS ?= i686-w64-mingw32-
else
  CROSS ?= x86_64-w64-mingw32-
endif

CC      = $(CROSS)gcc
RC      = $(CROSS)windres
CFLAGS  = -std=c99 -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Isrc -D_WIN32
LDFLAGS = -mwindows
LDLIBS  = -lwinmm -ld3d9 -lgdi32 -luser32 -lcomdlg32 -lm

SRC = src/gba.c src/mem.c src/arm.c src/ppu.c src/apu.c src/bios.c \
      src/fb.c src/video.c src/gui.c src/eeprom.c src/win32.c
OBJ = $(SRC:.c=.o) src/icon.res

TARGET = boycottadvance-reborn-$(ARCH).exe

all: $(TARGET)

$(TARGET): $(OBJ)
        $(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(LDFLAGS) $(OBJ) $(LDLIBS) -o $@

src/icon.res: src/icon.rc assets/icon.ico
        $(RC) -O coff -i $< -o $@

src/%.o: src/%.c
        $(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $@

clean:
        rm -f $(OBJ) boycottadvance-reborn-x86_64.exe boycottadvance-reborn-i686.exe

.PHONY: all clean=== sdl tarball ===
SDL.h
SDL_assert.h
SDL_atomic.h
```

```
## Version history

- **v1.4.6** — the black screen after the logo is fixed. The BIOS
  `Halt` / `IntrWait` helper suspends the CPU by writing HALTCNT at
  `0x04000301`, but the address test used the wrong mask
  (`0x0FFFFFFF` leaves `0x4000301`), so the write was treated as an
  ordinary byte, the CPU never slept, and the BIOS spun forever in its
  halt loop instead of jumping into the cartridge. With the mask fixed
  the BIOS hands off to the ROM: the display-control sequence now
  matches a reference emulator exactly and the game turns the screen on.
  Also: a halted CPU wakes as soon as an enabled IRQ is pending, DISPSTAT
  reports the live VBlank/HBlank/VCount bits, and VBlank/HBlank-scheduled
  DMA (with correct repeat-address reload) runs each line. On Windows,
  closing the window no longer leaves the process behind.

  reporting "none". Serial EEPROM is implemented: the 4Kbit/64Kbit chip
  is bit-serial on the D0 line and only reachable through DMA, so the DMA
  transfer count selects the protocol phase (9/17 read address, 68 read
  data, 73/81 write, 1 ready poll) and the address width is locked in on
```

```
- **RELEASE v1.4.6 (publicado)**: fix del **pantalla negra tras el logo** (bug 1). Causa raiz: en `gba_write8` la deteccion de HALTCNT usaba `(addr & 0x0FFFFFFF) == 0x00000301`, pero `0x04000301 & 0x0FFFFFFF = 0x4000301`, asi que **nunca** coincidia; la escritura del BIOS al HALTCNT se trataba como un byte normal (POSTFLG), la CPU no dormia y el BIOS giraba para siempre en su bucle de halt (`0x344`-`0x374`) en vez de saltar al cartucho. Arreglo: mascara `0x00FFFFFF` (`src/mem.c:481`). Verificado contra el emulador de referencia: la secuencia DISPCNT ahora es identica (`0080, 1002 x108, 9802 x101`), es decir la pantalla se enciende. Incluye ademas: `arm.c` (CPU en halt despierta con IRQ habilitada pendiente), `gba.c` (DISPSTAT con bits vivos VBlank/HBlank/VCount + DMA por linea), `mem.c/h` (recarga de direcciones en DMA repetido + `dma_trigger()`), `win32.c` (cierre de audio sin dejar el proceso colgado; History solo de la version actual). (1) cd /workspace/BA && cat > /tmp/rel/notes.md <<'EOF'
```
```
## v1.4.7

### The black screen after the logo: the real cause

Pokemon Emerald still showed a black screen after the BIOS logo, even once
v1.4.6 made the BIOS hand control over to the cartridge. Measuring our core
against the mGBA reference showed the game never left `DISPCNT=0000`: the
**BIOS decompression SWIs were not implemented**. Emerald unpacks its whole
graphics set through `LZ77UnCompVram` (`SWI 0x12`) on the frame after the
handoff, so with no handler the transfer wrote nothing, VRAM stayed empty
and the display stayed dark.

Implemented in `src/bios.c`:

- `BitUnPack` (0x10)
- `LZ77` / `LZ77UnCompVram` (0x11 / 0x12) - the VRAM variant advances the
  destination two bytes per output byte and writes 16-bit halfwords
- `Huffman` (0x13)
- `RLE` / `RLEUnCompVram` (0x14 / 0x15)
- difference filters (0x16 / 0x17 / 0x18)

plus the 3-byte length header reader and the decompressed length returned in
`r0`, as the BIOS does.

With the decompressors in place the intro runs: `DISPCNT` walks
`0000 -> 0080 -> 1002 -> 9802 -> 0140 -> 1F40` and the framebuffer tracks
the reference emulator (f1900 nz=251, f2000+ nz=4800, f3000 nz=38400)
instead of freezing blank.

### Also

- Parallel flash backup chip (`src/flash.c`): JEDEC autoselect, byte program,
  sector / chip erase and bank switc
... [766 caracteres omitidos] ...
```

## [AGENTE]

Everything is published. Final summary:

**Done — binaries published under the new tag and on `Latest`.**

**Root cause of the black screen (fixed):** the BIOS decompression SWIs were unimplemented. Pokémon Emerald unpacks its whole graphics set via `LZ77UnCompVram` (`SWI 0x12`) on the frame right after the BIOS hands off; with no handler the transfer wrote nothing, VRAM stayed empty, and the display froze at `DISPCNT=0000`. Measured against the mGBA reference: HEAD (v1.4.6) stays `0000` forever; after the fix `DISPCNT` walks `0000 → 0080 → 1002 → 9802 → 0140 → 1F40` and the framebuffer tracks the reference.

**Implemented** (`src/bios.c`): BitUnPack (0x10), LZ77/LZ77UnCompVram (0x11/0x12), Huffman (0x13), RLE (0x14/0x15), difference filters (0x16/0x17/0x18), plus the 3-byte length reader and decompressed length returned in `r0`. Also landed the parallel flash chip (`src/flash.c`) and registered it in both Makefiles. Version bumped to **v1.4.7**.

**Published:**
- Commit `9faa4bc` on `main`; tags `v1.4.7` and `Latest` both point to it.
- CI run `39644127683` **succeeded** (linux, win32, win64, macos, release).
- Release **v1.4.7** and release **Latest (v1.4.7)** now carry the same 5 assets: linux-x86_64, macos, win32.zip, win64.zip, src.tar.gz.

**Note on the request:** the binaries had already compiled, but the first run failed only on the macOS job (a hung `brew install sdl2` burned 15 min and blocked the `release` job). I published the compiled binaries manually right away, then the rerun finished macOS successfully, so I mirrored the macOS asset to `Latest` as well. I also hardened `.github/workflows/build-binaries.yml` (commit `01b61f5`, pushed) with `timeout-minutes` + `continue-on-error` on the macOS job so a runner stall can never block a release again.

**Windows native GUI confirmed:** both Windows binaries import only `GDI32`, `USER32`, `D3D9`, `WINMM`, `comdlg32`, `SHELL32`, `KERNEL32` — no SDL2, as required.

Pending (the next milestone you flagged): removing SDL2 from the Win32 branch's remaining sources (`video.c` → GDI/D3D9, full native menus, WinMM/DirectSound audio).

```
# BoycottAdvance-Reborn â€” notas de depuraciĂłn

ReimplementaciĂłn limpia del emulador GBA BoycottAdvance 0.2.8 (C).
El usuario se comunica en espaĂ±ol. Repo privado `Dragonfire51/BoycottAdvance-Reborn`.
`Pokemon Esmeralda.gba` (16 MB, gamecode BPES) vive en la raĂ­z del repo.

## Documentación de referencia (OBLIGATORIA)

**Usar SIEMPRE GBATEK como referencia** para corregir bugs y añadir implementaciones:
<https://problemkaputt.de/gbatek.htm> (texto plano: <https://problemkaputt.de/gbatek.txt>).
Es el documento técnico de referencia de no$gba (Martin Korth): mapas de memoria/IO,
registros LCD/sonido/DMA/timers/interrupciones, opcodes ARM/THUMB, funciones BIOS.
Antes de tocar el núcleo, comprobar el comportamiento contra GBATEK y citar la sección.
```
