=== swi dispatch ===
void gba_swi(GBA *g, uint32_t comment) {
    uint32_t swi_num = comment & 0xFF;

    /* Advance the program counter past the SWI instruction before running
       the handler. Handlers such as Halt/IntrWait set cst.halt, which the
       frame loop then uses to sleep the CPU until the next interrupt. */
    if (thumb_mode_p(g)) g->cpu.r[15] += 2;
    else                 g->cpu.r[15] += 4;

    switch (swi_num) {
    case 0x00: swi_soft_reset(g); break;
    case 0x01: swi_register_ram_reset(g); break;
    case 0x02: swi_halt(g); break;
    case 0x03: swi_stop(g); break;
    case 0x04: swi_intr_wait(g); break;
    case 0x05: swi_vblank_intr_wait(g); break;
    case 0x06: swi_div32(g); break;
    case 0x07: swi_div_arm(g); break;
    case 0x08: swi_sqrt(g); break;
    case 0x0B: swi_cpu_set(g); break;
    case 0x0C: swi_cpu_fast_set(g); break;
    case 0x0E: swi_affine_set(g); break;
    case 0x0F: swi_obj_affine_set(g); break;
    case 0x10: swi_bitunpack(g); break;
    case 0x11: swi_lz77(g, false); break;
    case 0x12: swi_lz77(g, true); break;
    case 0x13: swi_huffuncomp(g); break;
    case 0x14: swi_rluncomp(g, false); break;
    case 0x15: swi_rluncomp(g, true); break;
    case 0x16: swi_diffunfilter(g, false, false); break;
    case 0x17: swi_diffunfilter(g, true,  false); break;

uint32_t gba_read32(GBA *g, uint32_t addr) {
    switch (addr >> 24) {
    case 0x00: return rd32_al(g->bios + (addr & 0x3FFC));
    case 0x02: return rd32_al(g->ewram + (addr & 0x3FFFC));
    case 0x03: return rd32_al(g->iwram + (addr & 0x7FFC));
    case 0x04: return io_read16(g, addr & ~3u) | ((uint32_t)io_read16(g, (addr & ~3u) + 2) << 16);
    case 0x05: return rd32_al(g->pal + (addr & 0x3FC));
    case 0x06: { uint32_t o = addr & 0x1FFFC; if (o >= 0x18000) o -= 0x8000; return rd32_al(g->vram + o); }
    case 0x07: return rd32_al(g->oam + (addr & 0x3FC));
    case 0x08: case 0x09: case 0x0A: case 0x0B: case 0x0C: case 0x0D: {
        if (eeprom_addr_in_range(g, addr)) return 0;  /* EEPROM: bit-serie, solo por DMA de 16 bit */
        uint32_t a = addr & ~3u;
        return (uint32_t)rom_read16(g, a) | ((uint32_t)rom_read16(g, a + 2) << 16);
    }
    case 0x0E: case 0x0F: return (uint32_t)backup_read8(g, addr) * 0x01010101u;
    default: return 0;
    }
}

uint16_t gba_read16(GBA *g, uint32_t addr) {
    switch (addr >> 24) {
    case 0x00: return rd16_al(g->bios + (addr & 0x3FFE));
    case 0x02: return rd16_al(g->ewram + (addr & 0x3FFFE));
    case 0x03: return rd16_al(g->iwram + (addr & 0x7FFE));
    case 0x04: return io_read16(g, addr);

void arm_execute(GBA *g, uint32_t max_cycles) {
    uint32_t start = g->cycle;
    while (g->cycle - start < max_cycles) {
        /* SWI 04h/05h (IntrWait/VBlankIntrWait): only the awaited IRQ releases
           the halt.  Unrelated IRQs are ignored by the BIOS wait loop, so the
           game handler must not run while we are waiting (GBATEK SWI 04h/05h). */
        if (g->cst.halt && g->cst.wait_mask) {
            if (g->if_reg & g->cst.wait_mask) {
                uint16_t done = g->cst.wait_mask;
                g->cst.wait_mask = 0;
                g->cst.halt = false;
                /* Leave the awaited flag set: the game's own IRQ/VBlank
                   handler (running after the SWI returns) clears it. */
                (void)done;
            } else {
                g->cycle = start + max_cycles;      /* duerme hasta la IRQ esperada */
                break;
            }
        }

        /* Una CPU en halt despierta en cuanto hay una IRQ habilitada (IE & IF),
           sin importar IME ni el bit I del CPSR; IME/I solo gobiernan el salto al vector. */
        if (g->cst.halt && (g->if_reg & g->ie & 0x3FFF)) g->cst.halt = false;

static void arm_exec_at(GBA *g, uint32_t insn) {
    uint32_t cpsr = get_cpsr(g);
    uint32_t cond = insn >> 28;
    if (!cond_holds(cpsr, cond)) { set_pc(g, r15(g) + 4); add_cycles(g, 1); return; }

    uint32_t op  = (insn >> 25) & 0x7;
    bool     i   = (insn >> 25) & 1;
    bool     p   = (insn >> 24) & 1, u = (insn >> 23) & 1, b = (insn >> 22) & 1, w = (insn >> 21) & 1;
    bool     l   = (insn >> 20) & 1;
    int      rn  = (insn >> 16) & 0xF, rd = (insn >> 12) & 0xF;

    /* ---- SWI: bits 27-24 = 1111 (comentario de 24 bit; la BIOS GBA usa bits 23-16) ---- */
    if ((insn & 0x0F000000u) == 0x0F000000u) {
        gba_swi(g, (insn >> 16) & 0xFF);

uint32_t gba_read32(GBA *g, uint32_t addr) {
    switch (addr >> 24) {
    case 0x00: return rd32_al(g->bios + (addr & 0x3FFC));
    case 0x02: return rd32_al(g->ewram + (addr & 0x3FFFC));
    case 0x03: return rd32_al(g->iwram + (addr & 0x7FFC));
    case 0x04: return io_read16(g, addr & ~3u) | ((uint32_t)io_read16(g, (addr & ~3u) + 2) << 16);
    case 0x05: return rd32_al(g->pal + (addr & 0x3FC));
    case 0x06: { uint32_t o = addr & 0x1FFFC; if (o >= 0x18000) o -= 0x8000; return rd32_al(g->vram + o); }
    case 0x07: return rd32_al(g->oam + (addr & 0x3FC));

    }
    case 0x0E: case 0x0F: return (uint32_t)backup_read8(g, addr) * 0x01010101u;
    default: return 0;
    }
}

    uint32_t swi_num = comment & 0xFF;

format binary as 'gba'

include '../lib/constants.inc'
include '../lib/macros.inc'

macro m_exit test {
        mov     r12, test
        b       eval
}

header:
        include '../lib/header.asm'

main:
        m_test_init

        ; Reset test register
        mov     r12, 0

t001:
        ; BIOS read returns 0x0DC+8 after startup
        mov     r0, 0
        m_word  r1, 0xE129F000
        ldr     r2, [r0]
        cmp     r2, r1
        bne     f001
        b       t002

f001:
        m_exit  1

t002:
        ; BIOS read returns 0x188+8 after SWI
        mov     r0, 0
        m_word  r2, 0xE3A02004
        swi     0x80000  ; sqrt(r0)
        ldr     r3, [r0]
        cmp     r3, r2
        bne     f002
        b       t003

f002:
        m_exit  2

t003:
        ; BIOS read returns 0x134+8 during IRQ
        adr     r0, .isr
        m_word  r1, 0x03007FFC
        str     r0, [r1]

        ; Enable interrupts
        mov     r0, STAT_VBLANK_IRQ
        mov     r1, MEM_IO
        mov     r2, REG_DISPSTAT
        strh    r0, [r1, r2]
        mov     r0, IRQ_VBLANK
        mov     r2, REG_IE
        strh    r0, [r1, r2]
        mov     r0, 1
        mov     r2, REG_IME
        strh    r0, [r1, r2]

        ; Wait for vblank
        m_vsync

        ; Disable interrupts
        mov     r0, 0
        mov     r1, MEM_IO
        mov     r2, REG_IME
        strh    r0, [r1, r2]

}
/* Minimal BIOS HLE for the interrupt vectors.  A real BIOS maps its default
 * IRQ handler at address 0x18 and, around entry, reads the address stored at
 * 0x03FFFFFC as the IRQ dispatcher pointer.  When no BIOS dump is loaded we
 * install a tiny stub in IWRAM (the BIOS shadow region is beyond the ARM7's
 * 0x03FF0000-0x03FFFFFF area) so an interrupt taken before the game installs
 * its own handler returns immediately instead of executing empty space.
 *
 * The stub must be DMA-ed into IWRAM because code cannot normally be written
 * there via normal 16/32-bit stores at 0x03000000+ (the game is still running
 * from a low address and has full access).  Practically we place it at the
 * very top of IWRAM (0x03007F00) which BIOS-driven code typically treats as
 * scratch.
 */
static void bios_write32(uint8_t *dst, uint32_t v) {
    dst[0] = (uint8_t)(v & 0xFF);
    dst[1] = (uint8_t)((v >> 8) & 0xFF);
    dst[2] = (uint8_t)((v >> 16) & 0xFF);
    dst[3] = (uint8_t)((v >> 24) & 0xFF);
}

void arm_exec(GBA *g) {

/* ===================================================================== */
/* Thumb mode interpreter (ARMv4T), decodificado por los bits 15-12      */
/* ===================================================================== */
static void thumb_exec_at(GBA *g, uint16_t insn) {
    uint32_t cpsr = get_cpsr(g);
    uint32_t op = insn >> 12;
    uint32_t rd = insn & 7, rs = (insn >> 3) & 7, rn = (insn >> 6) & 7;
    uint32_t next = r15(g) + 2;

    /* formato 2: add/subtract (00011) */
    if ((insn & 0xF800) == 0x1800) {
        bool immf = insn & 0x0400;
        bool sub  = insn & 0x0200;
        uint32_t b = immf ? ((insn >> 6) & 7) : read_reg(g, rn);
        uint32_t a = read_reg(g, rs);
        uint32_t r = sub ? a - b : a + b;
        if (sub) flags_sub3(g, a, b, r, 1); else flags_add3(g, a, b, r, 0);
        write_reg(g, rd, r);
        set_pc(g, next); add_cycles(g, 1); return;
    }

    /* formato 1: move shifted register */
    if (op == 0x0 || op == 0x1) {

    uint32_t start = g->cycle;

static inline void bios_track_fetch(GBA *g) {
    uint32_t pc = g->cpu.r[15];
    if ((pc >> 24) == 0) {
        g->bios_last_pc = pc;
    } else if (g->bios_last_pc != 0xFFFFFFFFu) {
        uint32_t src = (g->bios_last_pc + 8u) & 0x3FFCu;
        g->bios_prefetch = g->bios[src] | ((uint32_t)g->bios[src + 1] << 8) |
                           ((uint32_t)g->bios[src + 2] << 16) |
                           ((uint32_t)g->bios[src + 3] << 24);
        g->bios_last_pc = 0xFFFFFFFFu;
    }
}
static inline void add_cycles(GBA *g, uint32_t n) { g->cycle += n; }

void gba_load_bios(GBA *g, const char *path) {
    FILE *f = fopen(path, "rb");
    if (!f) return;
    size_t got = fread(g->bios, 1, BIOS_SIZE, f);
    if (got < BIOS_SIZE) memset(g->bios + got, 0, BIOS_SIZE - got);
    fclose(f);
    g->bios_enabled = true;
    g->bios_loaded = (got == BIOS_SIZE);
}

bool gba_load_rom(GBA *g, const char *path) {
    FILE *f = fopen(path, "rb");
    if (!f) return false;
    fseek(f, 0, SEEK_END);
    long sz = ftell(f);
    fseek(f, 0, SEEK_SET);
    if (sz <= 0 || sz > ROM_MAX) { fclose(f); return false; }
    size_t got = fread(g->rom, 1, (size_t)sz, f);
    fclose(f);

+/* GBATEK: al salir de la BIOS, el prefetcher retiene la palabra que la BIOS
+   iba a ejecutar a continuacion (PC_BIOS + 8). Una lectura posterior a la BIOS
+   desde fuera de ella devuelve ese valor, no el contenido de la memoria. Se
+   comprobo contra mGBA: al saltar desde 0x0DC se retiene [0x0E4], desde 0x188
+   [0x190], desde 0x134 [0x13C] y desde 0x13C [0x144]. */
+static inline void bios_track_fetch(GBA *g) {
+    uint32_t pc = g->cpu.r[15];
+    if ((pc >> 24) == 0) {
+        g->bios_last_pc = pc;
+    } else if (g->bios_last_pc != 0xFFFFFFFFu) {
+        uint32_t src = (g->bios_last_pc + 8u) & 0x3FFCu;
+        g->bios_prefetch = g->bios[src] | ((uint32_t)g->bios[src + 1] << 8) |
+                           ((uint32_t)g->bios[src + 2] << 16) |
+                           ((uint32_t)g->bios[src + 3] << 24);
+        g->bios_last_pc = 0xFFFFFFFFu;
+    }
+}

endif
OBJ = $(SRC:.c=.o) $(ICON_OBJ)

all: boycottadvance-reborn

boycottadvance-reborn: $(OBJ)
        $(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(OBJ) $(LDLIBS) -o $@

src/icon.res: src/icon.rc assets/icon.ico
        $(RC) -O coff -i $< -o $@

clean:
        rm -f $(OBJ) boycottadvance-reborn

.PHONY: all clean
```

Both parts are done.

## 1. Commit + push (core accuracy fixes)

Committed as `8bb7802` and pushed to `main` (the "Latest" branch, no PR):

> **core: model BIOS prefetch latch on leave-BIOS (GBATEK); Thumb POP{} quirk**

- `arm.c` — `bios_track_fetch()` latches `BIOS[last_BIOS_pc + 8]` when the CPU leaves the BIOS region; wired into `arm_exec()` / `thumb_exec()`.
- `mem.c` — BIOS `read32` returns the latched word once outside the BIOS.
- `bios.c` — HLE SWI pins the latch to the `0x188+8` word (`E3A02004`); HLE stub gains the `0x144` word for the IRQ-return path.
- `gba.c` — reset seeds the latch from the reset vector (`0x0DC+8`).
- `arm.c` — Thumb `POP {}` applies the ARM7TDMI quirk (R15 loaded, SP += 0x40).

**gba-tests: 73 passed / 51 failed / 9 unknown** — up from 61 passing, zero regressions. `bios`, `start_up`, `prefetcher_*` and `dma_from_bios` now pass.

Note on the timer work: I reverted the lazy per-instruction timer sync. Making the counter advance after each instruction changed IRQ timing globally and dropped the suite to 42 passing, and the bulk-ahead model can't be projected accurately without a full per-cycle rework. The `Pop_no_regs` failure is a timer cycle-timing artifact, not the instruction semantics — the POP quirk itself is correct and preserved.

  por `uint16_t cst.wait_mask`. **Solo la SWI que se espera despierta a la CPU**: `swi_intr_wait`
  (0x04) pone `wait_mask=r1&0x3FFF`; `swi_vblank_intr_wait` (0x05) `wait_mask=IF_VBLANK`;
  `Halt`/`Stop`/HALTCNT directo ponen `wait_mask=0` (cualquier IRQ despierta, GBATEK). En
  `arm_execute()`, una CPU halteada con `wait_mask!=0` solo despierta cuando el flag esperado
  llega; si no, duerme el resto del frame. Antes, cualquier IRQ (p.ej. timer/serial) hacia
  reintentar el bucle del BIOS una vez por scanline y el reloj percibido se destemplaba.

include 'constants.inc'

macro m_half reg, value {
        mov     reg, value and 0xFF
        orr     reg, value and 0xFF00
}

macro m_word reg, value {
        mov     reg, value and 0xFF
        orr     reg, value and 0xFF00
        orr     reg, value and 0xFF0000
        orr     reg, value and 0xFF000000
}

macro m_vsync {
local .vblank_end
local .vblank_beg

        stmfd   sp!, \{r0-r1\}
        mov     r0, MEM_IO

.vblank_end:
        ldr     r1, [r0, REG_DISPSTAT]
        tst     r1, STAT_VBLANK_FLG
        bne     .vblank_end             ; Loop until not in vblank

.vblank_beg:
        ldr     r1, [r0, REG_DISPSTAT]
        tst     r1, STAT_VBLANK_FLG
        beq     .vblank_beg             ; Loop until in vblank
        ldmfd   sp!, \{r0-r1\}
}

macro m_text_init {
        bl      text_init
}

macro m_text_color color, index {
        m_half  r0, color
        mov     r1, index
        bl      text_color
}

macro m_text_pos x, y {
        mov     r0, x
        mov     r1, y
}

macro m_text_char char {
        mov     r2, char
        bl      text_char
}

macro m_test_init {
        m_text_init
        m_text_color 0xFFFF, 0
        m_text_color 0x0000, 1
        m_text_color 0xFFFF, 2
}

        cmp     r0, 3
        bne     f001c

        ldm     r1, {r8, r9, r10}^
        ldm     r8, {r8, r9, r10}^
        ldr     r0, [r9, +r10]
        mov     r1, 0x100

        cmp     r0, r1
        bne     f001d

        mov     r12, 0
        bl      eval

.mode_data:
        dw      0xF0000011

.data_r8:
        dw      0x03000000


f001a:
        mov     r12, 1
        bl      eval

f001b:
        mov     r12, 2
        bl      eval

f001c:
        mov     r12, 3
        bl      eval

f001d:
        mov     r12, 4
        bl      eval

eval:
        mov     r0, r12
        mov     r1, 0x1F
        msr     cpsr, r1

        m_vsync
        m_test_eval r0

idle:
        b       idle

include '../lib/text.asm'

main_end:

void apu_mix(GBA *g, int16_t *stream, int nframes) {
    (void)g;
    unsigned rd = atomic_load_explicit(&ring_r, memory_order_relaxed);
    unsigned w  = atomic_load_explicit(&ring_w, memory_order_acquire);
    for (int i = 0; i < nframes; i++) {
        if (rd != w) {
            last_l = ring[(rd & (RING_FRAMES - 1)) * 2];
            last_r = ring[(rd & (RING_FRAMES - 1)) * 2 + 1];
            rd++;
        }                                                   /* vacio: se repite la ultima muestra */
        stream[i * 2]     = last_l;
        stream[i * 2 + 1] = last_r;
    }
    atomic_store_explicit(&ring_r, rd, memory_order_release);
}

/* Cuantas muestras hay listas para reproducir (utilidad de test). */
int apu_available(void) {
    unsigned w = atomic_load_explicit(&ring_w, memory_order_acquire);
    unsigned rd = atomic_load_explicit(&ring_r, memory_order_relaxed);
    return (int)(w - rd);
}

static void render_affine_bg(GBA *g, int bgn, int y) {
    Ppu *p = &g->ppu;
    uint16_t *out = lb.bg[bgn];
    int a = bgn - 2;
    uint16_t bgcnt = p->bgcnt[bgn];
    uint32_t cbb = ((bgcnt >> 2) & 3) * 0x4000;
    uint32_t sb  = ((bgcnt >> 8) & 0x1F) * 0x800;
    bool wrap = bgcnt & 0x2000;                     /* area overflow: wraparound */
    int dim = 128 << ((bgcnt >> 14) & 3);           /* 128/256/512/1024, square */
    int mos_h = 1, mos_v = 1;
    if (bgcnt & 0x40) {
        mos_h = (p->mosaic & 0xF) + 1;
        mos_v = ((p->mosaic >> 4) & 0xF) + 1;
    }
    int32_t pa = p->pa[a], pc = p->pc[a];
    int32_t rx = p->refx[a], ry = p->refy[a];
    if (mos_v > 1) ry -= p->pd[a] * (y % mos_v);    /* first line of the mosaic row */
    for (int x = 0; x < SCREEN_W; x++) {
        int xs = x - (x % mos_h);
        int32_t sx = (rx + pa * xs) >> 8;
        int32_t sy = (ry + pc * xs) >> 8;
        if (sx < 0 || sx >= dim || sy < 0 || sy >= dim) {
            if (!wrap) { out[x] = TRANS; continue; }
            sx &= dim - 1; sy &= dim - 1;
        }
        int tno = read_vram8(g, sb + (uint32_t)(sy >> 3) * (uint32_t)(dim >> 3) + (uint32_t)(sx >> 3));
        int idx = read_vram8(g, cbb + (uint32_t)tno * 64 + (uint32_t)(sy & 7) * 8 + (uint32_t)(sx & 7));
        out[x] = idx ? read_pal(g, idx) : TRANS;
    }
}

/* mode helpers (banked regs) */
static int bank_of(uint32_t cpsr) {
    switch (cpsr & 0x1F) {
    case 0x11: return BANK_FIQ;
    case 0x12: return BANK_IRQ;
    case 0x13: return BANK_SVC;
    case 0x17: return BANK_ABT;
    case 0x1B: return BANK_UND;
    default:   return BANK_USR;
    }
}

static void change_mode(GBA *g, uint32_t new_cpsr) {
    int ob = bank_of(get_cpsr(g)), nb = bank_of(new_cpsr);
    if (ob == nb) { set_cpsr(g, new_cpsr); return; }
    /* FIQ banks r8-r12 as well as r13/r14 (GBATEK "CPU Registers"). */
    if (ob == BANK_FIQ || nb == BANK_FIQ) {
        for (int i = 0; i < 5; i++) {
            uint32_t t = g->cpu.r[8 + i];
            g->cpu.r[8 + i] = g->cpu.bank[nb][i];
            g->cpu.bank[ob][i] = t;
        }
    }
    g->cpu.bank[ob][5] = g->cpu.r[13];
    g->cpu.bank[ob][6] = g->cpu.r[14];
    set_cpsr(g, new_cpsr);
    g->cpu.r[13] = g->cpu.bank[nb][5];
    g->cpu.r[14] = g->cpu.bank[nb][6];
}

void arm_set_mode(GBA *g, uint32_t mode) {
    change_mode(g, (get_cpsr(g) & ~0x1Fu) | mode);
}

static void enter_exception(GBA *g, uint32_t mode, uint32_t lr_val, uint32_t pc_addr) {
    uint32_t old = get_cpsr(g);
    g->cpu.spsr[bank_of(mode)] = old;               /* SPSR_<mode> = CPSR */
    /* Los vectores se ejecutan en estado ARM con IRQ deshabilitadas. */
    change_mode(g, (old & ~0x3Fu) | mode | CPSR_I);
    g->cpu.r[14] = lr_val;                          /* LR_<mode> */
    set_pc(g, pc_addr);
}

    a->sample_acc += (uint64_t)cycles * SAMPLE_RATE;

commit 8bb7802a6e44133fd23c05a2ccc09f35a69375be
Author: openhands <openhands@all-hands.dev>
Date:   Sat Oct 24 16:02:19 2026 +0000

    core: model BIOS prefetch latch on leave-BIOS (GBATEK); Thumb POP{} quirk

    GBATEK documents that the ARM7 prefetcher retains the word following the
    last instruction fetched inside the BIOS, and that a BIOS read issued from
    outside the region returns that retained word instead of memory contents.

    - arm.c: bios_track_fetch() latches BIOS[last_BIOS_pc + 8] when the CPU
      leaves the BIOS region; called from arm_exec() and thumb_exec().
    - mem.c: BIOS read32 returns the latched value once the CPU is outside.
    - bios.c: HLE SWI pins the latch to the 0x188+8 word (E3A02004) since the
      real BIOS vector is not executed; the HLE stub gains the 0x144 word that
      the IRQ return path retains.
    - gba.c: reset seeds the latch with the reset-vector value (0x0DC+8).
    - arm.c: Thumb POP with an empty register list now applies the ARM7TDMI
      quirk (transfers R15, SP += 0x40).

# Makefile.win32 - cross-compile the native Windows build (no SDL).
#
# The Windows build links directly to GDI / Direct3D 9 / waveOut (WinMM);
# SDL2 is intentionally not used. Build from Linux with a MinGW cross
# toolchain, or from Windows with MinGW-w64:
#
#   make -f Makefile.win32                     # x86_64, mingw64
#   make -f Makefile.win32 ARCH=i686           # i686, mingw32
#
# Variables:
#   CROSS  toolchain prefix (default: x86_64-w64-mingw32- / i686-w64-mingw32-)

ARCH ?= x86_64
ifeq ($(ARCH),i686)
  CROSS ?= i686-w64-mingw32-
else
  CROSS ?= x86_64-w64-mingw32-
endif

CC      = $(CROSS)gcc
RC      = $(CROSS)windres
CFLAGS  = -std=c99 -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Isrc -D_WIN32
LDFLAGS = -mwindows
LDLIBS  = -lwinmm -ld3d9 -lgdi32 -luser32 -lcomdlg32 -lm

SRC = src/gba.c src/mem.c src/arm.c src/ppu.c src/apu.c src/bios.c \
      src/fb.c src/video.c src/gui.c src/eeprom.c src/flash.c src/win32.c
OBJ = $(SRC:.c=.

def read_text(vram, y0, x0, n):
    out = []
    for c in range(n):
        x = x0 + c * 8
        blk = bytearray()
        for row in range(8):
            off = (y0 + row) * 240 + x
            blk += vram[off:off + 8]
        best, bestscore = "?", -1
        for pat, ch in GLYPHS.items():
            s = sum(1 for a, b in zip(pat, blk) if a == b)
            if s > bestscore:
                bestscore, best = s, ch
        out.append(best if bestscore >= 60 else "?")
    return "".join(out)


def verdict(prefix):
    try:
        vram = open(prefix + ".vram.bin", "rb").read()
    except OSError:
        return None
    txt = ""
    for x0 in (56, 60, 64, 40):
        t = read_text(vram, 76, x0, 32).replace("\x7f", " ")
        if "All tests passed" in t:
            return "PASS", ""
        m = re.search(r"Failed test (\d+)", t)
        if m:
            return "FAIL", m.group(1)
        if t.strip():
            txt = t
    return None, txt.strip()


def main():
    os.makedirs(OUT, exist_ok=True)
    roms = sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(ROOT, "**", "*.gba"), recursive=True))
    results = {}
    for rom in roms:
        name = os.path.relpath(rom, ROOT)
        pre = os.path.join(OUT, "cur")
        env = dict(os.environ, BIOS=BIOS)
        try:
            subprocess.run([HH, rom, str(FRAMES), "dump", pre],
                           capture_output=True, timeout=180, env=env)
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
            results[name] = ("TIMEOUT", "")

/* --------------------------------------------------------------- wndproc */
static LRESULT CALLBACK gui_wndproc(HWND h, UINT msg, WPARAM wp, LPARAM lp) {
    switch (msg) {
    case WM_COMMAND: {
        int id = LOWORD(wp);
        if (id && g_cb.action) {
            if (g_cb.pause_audio)  g_cb.pause_audio();
            g_cb.action(id);
            if (g_cb.resume_audio) g_cb.resume_audio();
            gui_native_sync();
        }
        return 0;
    }
    case WM_INITMENUPOPUP:
        gui_native_sync();
        break;
    case WM_CLOSE:
        g_quit = 1;
        break;
    }
    if (g_oldproc) return CallWindowProcW(g_oldproc, h, msg, wp, lp);
    return DefWindowProcW(h, msg, wp, lp);
}

static void gen_sample(Apu *a, int16_t *outl, int16_t *outr) {
    if (!a->master) { *outl = *outr = 0; return; }

    /* frame sequencer: 512 Hz = cada 32768 ciclos de CPU */
    a->fs_cc += STEP_FP;
    while (a->fs_cc >= (32768ULL << 16)) {
        a->fs_cc -= (32768ULL << 16);
        int s = a->fs_step;
        a->fs_step = (s + 1) & 7;
        if ((s & 1) == 0) clock_length(a);
        if (s == 2 || s == 6) clock_sweep(a);
        if (s == 7) clock_env(a);

/*
 * apu.c - GBA sound: 4 canales PSG + 2 FIFOs de Direct Sound (GBATEK "GBA Sound Controller").
 *
 * Diseno:
 *  - apu_step() lo llama el nucleo con los ciclos de CPU ejecutados y genera
 *    muestras a 44100 Hz en un ring buffer (productor = hilo de emulacion).
 *  - apu_mix() es el callback de SDL (consumidor): solo copia del ring buffer.
 *  - Los FIFOs avanzan con los desbordamientos de TIMER0/TIMER1 y piden datos
 *    por DMA (timing 3) cuando quedan <= 16 bytes, como el hardware.

## [AGENTE]

Todo verificado y publicado. Resumen final:

## Lo que se ejecutó en esta sesión

**1. El commit+push pendiente (que el hilo anterior no llegó a hacer) — HECHO**

Aclaración importante: el trabajo del D-pad POV **ya estaba commiteado y publicado** en una sesión previa (`a8c709f`, rama `joystick-dpad-pov`, ancestro de `main`). No quedaba nada de eso sin commitear. Lo que sí estaba sin commitear eran los cambios de harness, y encontré un bug real de build.

- `0263118` — **`build(win32): per-arch object dirs so x86 and x64 build in one tree`**
- `4958c79` — `docs(agents): mGBA frame-phase offset caveat; Win32 per-arch build notes`

Ambos publicados en `main` ("Latest") **sin PR**, como pediste. Árbol de trabajo limpio, todo en `origin/main`.

**2. Hito Win32 sin SDL — verificado completo, más un arreglo real**

El hito **ya estaba implementado y mergeado** en `main` (ramas `win32-native-no-sdl` y `22cb833`, ya ancestro de `main`). Lo verifiqué de punta a punta:

- `make -f Makefile.win32` (x86_64) y `ARCH=i686` (i686): **0 warnings** con `-Wall -Wextra`.
- Los `.exe` importan **solo** `comdlg32, d3d9, GDI32, KERNEL32, msvcrt, SHELL32, USER32, WINMM` — **cero símbolos SDL**.
- `WindowProc` completa (`wnd_proc` + `gui_wndproc` que intercepta `WM_COMMAND`/`WM_INITMENUPOPUP`), menú nativo completo (`File/Window/Options/Help` + `Controls → Input Configuration`), **Debug ausente** como pediste, audio por `waveOut` (WinMM), vídeo GDI (`StretchDIBits`) + D3D9.

**Bug real encontrado y arreglado:** el link de i686 fallaba con *"file format not recognized"* porque ambas arquitecturas escribían sus `.o` en los mismos `src/*.o`. Ahora van a `build/$(ARCH)/`.

**3. Diagnóstico gráfico — corregí dos conclusiones erróneas previas**

- El supuesto **"byte-swap de OAM bytes 6/7"** era un **artefacto**: comparábamos contra un frame de mGBA **congelado/obsoleto**. La ruta de OAM en `mem.c` es little-endian correcta.
- El harness de mGBA va **sistemáticamente por detrás** en las transiciones de carga (nuestra f900 Esmeralda == mGBA f920; nuestra f600 Medabots == mGBA f606), y mGBA congela la pantalla f744→f760.
- **Medabots AX es pixel-perfect (0.00%) cada 40 frames** (f650, 690, 730, 770…): es desfase de fase de animación, **no** un bug de render.

## Pendiente real (no abordado)

- **Análisis de sonido**: requiere un volcado de audio en `tools/headharness.c` (usando `apu_drain()`, que ya existe) y compararlo con `mGBA` para localizar el timbre incorrecto. No llegué a implementarlo.
- **Fallos de suite restantes** (51, baseline idéntico sin regresiones): el bloque grande son los `LDM/*` e `irq/*` (timing de ciclos internos), más los 4 que citas (DMA_pause_timing_ROM_to_IWRAM, serial_read_data, nes, dma_long).

Nota de fiabilidad: el transporte de tool calls funcionó con normalidad en toda esta sesión, a diferencia de la anterior.

void apu_step(GBA *g, uint32_t cycles) {
    Apu *a = &g->apu;
    a->sample_acc += (uint64_t)cycles * SAMPLE_RATE;
    while (a->sample_acc >= CPU_HZ) {
        a->sample_acc -= CPU_HZ;
        int16_t l, r;
        gen_sample(a, &l, &r);
        ring_push(l, r);
    }
}

/* waveOut playback of the stream the APU mixer produces. A short ringing
 * buffer keeps the callback latency reasonable without dropping beats. */
#define AUDIO_FREQ 44100
#define AUDIO_CHANNELS 2
#define AUDIO_SAMPLES 1024          /* per fragment */
#define AUDIO_FRAGS   6

typedef struct {
    HWAVEOUT  hwo;
    WAVEHDR   hdr[AUDIO_FRAGS];
    int16_t  *buf[AUDIO_FRAGS];
    int       cur;
    volatile int closing;   /* set before shutdown so the callback stops requeueing */
} Audio;
static Audio g_audio;

static void CALLBACK wave_proc(HWAVEOUT hwo, UINT uMsg, DWORD_PTR inst,
                               DWORD_PTR p1, DWORD_PTR p2) {
    (void)hwo; (void)p1; (void)p2;
    if (uMsg != WOM_DONE) return;
    Audio *a = (Audio *)inst;
    /* During shutdown the buffers must not be re-queued, otherwise
       waveOutReset can never drain and waveOutClose deadlocks. */
    if (a->closing) return;
    /* Mix in fresh audio for the finished fragment. */
    if (cfg.sound_enable && g) {
        apu_mix(g, a->buf[a->cur], AUDIO_SAMPLES);
        if (cfg.reverse_stereo)
            for (int i = 0; i < AUDIO_SAMPLES; i++) {
                int16_t l = a->buf[a->cur][i*2];
                a->buf[a->cur][i*2] = a->buf[a->cur][i*2+1];
                a->buf[a->cur][i*2+1] = l;
            }
    } else {
        memset(a->buf[a->cur], 0, (size_t)AUDIO_SAMPLES * 2 * sizeof(int16_t));
    }
    waveOutWrite(hwo, &a->hdr[a->cur], sizeof(WAVEHDR));
    a->cur = (a->cur + 1) % AUDIO_FRAGS

while (running) {
        while (PeekMessageW(&msg, NULL, 0, 0, PM_REMOVE)) {
            TranslateMessage(&msg);
            DispatchMessageW(&msg);
            if (msg.message == WM_QUIT) running = 0;
        }
        if (g_quit) break;

        poll_joy_capture();

        /* Run one frame. */
        if (!g_paused && g->rom_size > 0) {
            gba_update_keypad(g, key_state());
            gba_run_frame(g);
        }

        /* Recreate the framebuffer and presenter on demand. */
        RECT rc; GetClientRect(g_hwnd, &rc);
        int cw = rc.right - rc.left, ch = rc.bottom - rc.top;
        if (cw < 1) cw = 1;
        if (ch < 1) ch = 1;
        if (fb_w != cw || fb_h != ch) {
            if (fb_w) fb_free(&fb);
            fb_init(&fb, cw, ch);
            fb_w = cw; fb_h = ch;
        }
        if (want_backend != cfg.video_backend || !video) {
            if (video) vid_shutdown(video);
            video = vid_init((void *)g_hwnd, (VidBackend)cfg.video_backend);

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Compare our core framebuffer (RGB555 screen.bin) against mGBA PPM.

Usage: fb_diff.py <our_screen.bin> <ref.ppm> [--save map.ppm]

Both render the same ROM after the same number of frames. The reference PPM is
written by mgbaharness with mColor 0x00BBGGRR, our screen.bin is RGB555 with R
in bits 0-4. We expand both to 8-bit RGB and compare per-pixel.
"""
import sys

def load_ppm(path):
    with open(path, "rb") as f:
        data = f.read()
    # P6\nW H\n255\n
    parts = data.split(b"\n", 3)
    assert parts[0] == b"P6", "not P6"
    w, h = map(int, parts[1].split())
    assert w == 240 and h == 160, f"unexpected dims {w}x{h}"
    px = parts[3]
    return px, w, h

def load_rgb555(path):
    with open(path, "rb") as f:
        data = f.read()
    assert len(data) == 240 * 160 * 2, f"screen.bin size {len(data)}"
    out = bytearray(240 * 160 * 3)
    for i in range(240 * 160):
        c = data[2 * i] | (data[2 * i + 1] << 8)
        r = c & 0x1F
```

void dma_run(GBA *g, int ch) {
    DmaChan *d = &g->dma[ch];
    if (!d->enabled) return;

    /* Timing 3 en DMA1/2 = modo FIFO de sonido: siempre 4 palabras de 32 bit,
       destino fijo, el contador DMAxCNT_L se ignora. */
    bool fifo = (d->timing == 3) && (ch == 1 || ch == 2);
    uint32_t unit = (d->word || fifo) ? 4 : 2;
    uint32_t count;
    if (fifo) count = 4;
    else if (ch == 3) { count = d->count & 0xFFFF; if (!count) count = 0x10000; }
    else              { count = d->count & 0x3FFF; if (!count) count = 0x4000; }

    uint32_t src = d->src & ~(unit - 1);
    uint32_t dst = d->dst & ~(unit - 1);

    /* EEPROM es bit-serie y solo accesible por DMA de 16 bit: el recuento le dice
       en que fase del protocolo esta. */
    if (g->save_type == SAVE_EEPROM && !fifo && !d->word &&
        (eeprom_addr_in_range(g, dst) || eeprom_addr_in_range(g, src)))
        eeprom_dma_begin(g, count);

    for (uint32_t i = 0; i < count; i++) {
        if (unit == 4) gba_write32(g, dst, gba_read32(g, src));
        else           gba_write16(g, dst, gba_read16(g, src));
        /* src: 0 incrementa, 1 decrementa, 2 fijo, 3 prohibido (se trata como incremento) */
        if (d->src_ctl == 1) src -= unit;
        else if (d->src_ctl != 2) src += unit;
        /* dst: 0 incrementa, 1 decrementa, 2 fijo, 3 incrementa + recarga al repetir */
        if (!fifo) {
            if (d->dst_ctl == 1) dst -= unit;
            else if (d->dst_ctl != 2) dst += unit;
        }
    }
    d

    /* SWI 0x01: clear the memory regions selected by r0 and force the display
       into forced blank. Mirrors the hardware behaviour that games rely on to
       reinitialise their own shadow of the video registers. */
    uint32_t flags = g->cpu.r[0];

static void compose_frame(FB *fb, float fps) {
    fb_fill(fb, 0xFF000000);
    int aw = fb->w, ah = fb->h;
    /* Scale factor that keeps the 3:2 aspect. "Fit to window" uses the
     * largest whole multiple; a fixed zoom is reduced when the client area
     * is smaller, so the picture is never cropped. */
    double s;
    if (cfg.scalemode == 1) {
        double sx = (double)aw / SCREEN_W, sy = (double)ah / SCREEN_H;
        s = sx < sy ? sx : sy;
    } else {
        s = cfg.zoom;
        double sx = (double)aw / SCREEN_W, sy = (double)ah / SCREEN_H;
        double lim = sx < sy ? sx : sy;
        if (s > lim) s = lim;
    }
    int dstw = (int)(SCREEN_W * s), dsth = (int)(SCREEN_H * s);
    if (dstw < 1) dstw = 1;
    if (dsth < 1) dsth = 1;
    int dstx = (aw - dstw) / 2, dsty = (ah - dsth) / 2;
    fb_blit_frame(fb, dstx, dsty, dstw, dsth, g->ppu.frame, cfg.scanline);

    if (cfg.showfps) {
        char t[64];
        if (cfg.showfps_pct) snprintf(t,sizeof t,"%d%%",(int)(fps*100.0/59.7275));
        else snprintf(t,sizeof t,"%.0f fps",fps);
        fb_text(fb, fb->w-(int)strlen(t)*8-6, 4, t, 0xFFFFFF00);
    }
}

/* Native Windows: the framebuffer is StretchDIBits'd into the window DC. */

#if defined(_WIN32)
typedef struct { HWND hwnd; HDC hdc; BITMAPINFO bmi; } GdiState;

static int gdi_init(Video *v) {
    GdiState *g = (GdiState *)calloc(1, sizeof(GdiState));
    g->hwnd = (HWND)v->win;   /* native frontend passes its HWND */
    if (!g->hwnd) { free(g); return -1; }
    g->hdc = GetDC(g->hwnd);
    if (!g->hdc) { free(g); return -1; }
    memset(&g->bmi, 0, sizeof(g->bmi));
    g->bmi.bmiHeader.biSize = sizeof(BITMAPINFOHEADER);
    g->bmi.bmiHeader.biPlanes = 1;
    g->bmi.bmiHeader.biBitCount = 32;
    g->bmi.bmiHeader.biCompression = BI_RGB;
    v->native = g;
    return 0;
}
static void gdi_present(Video *v, const uint32_t *argb, int w, int h) {
    GdiState *g = (GdiState *)v->native;
    RECT rc; GetClientRect(g->hwnd, &rc);
    int cw = rc.right - rc.left, ch = rc.bottom - rc.top;
    g->bmi.bmiHeader.biWidth = w;
    g->bmi.bmiHeader.biHeight = -h;   /* top-down */
    StretchDIBits(g->hdc, 0, 0, cw, ch, 0, 0, w, h, argb, &g->bmi, DIB_RGB_COLORS, SRCCOPY);
}
static void gdi_shutdown(Video *v) {
    GdiState *g = (GdiState *)v->native;
    if (g) { if (g->hdc) ReleaseDC(g->hwnd, g->hdc); free(g); }
}
#endif /* _WIN32 */

- **Ambos reconvergen**: Medabots AX da 0.00% exacto en f300-f410 y en f460-f570;
  Esmeralda 0.00% en f680-f748. Por tanto un diff grande en un frame concreto NO

/* Tras restaurar el CPSR desde SPSR el PC debe alinearse segun el estado resultante. */
/* User-bank view of a register, for LDM/STM with the S bit and no PC in the
 * list: the transfer uses the User mode registers, not the current bank
 * (GBATEK "ARM Block Data Transfer"; gba-tests #511/#512). */
static uint32_t user_reg(GBA *g, int k) {
    if (bank_of(get_cpsr(g)) != BANK_USR && k >= 8 && k <= 14)
        return g->cpu.bank[BANK_USR][k - 8];
    return k == 15 ? r15(g) + 12 : g->cpu.r[k];
}
static void set_user_reg(GBA *g, int k, uint32_t v) {
    if (bank_of(get_cpsr(g)) != BANK_USR && k >= 8 && k <= 14) {
        g->cpu.bank[BANK_USR][k - 8] = v;
        return;
    }
    if (k == 15) set_pc(g, v & ~3u);
    else         g->cpu.r[k] = v;
}

static void branch_restore(GBA *g, uint32_t target) {
    set_pc(g, target & (thumb_mode(g) ? ~1u : ~3u));
}

    out = []

        x = x0 + c * 8
        blk = bytearray()
        for row in range(8):
            off = (y0 + row) * 240 + x
            blk += vram[off:off + 8]
        best, bestscore = "?", -1
        for pat, ch in GLYPHS.items():
            s = sum(1 for a, b in zip(pat, blk) if a == b)
            if s > bestscore:
                bestscore, best = s, ch
        out.append(best if bestscore >= 60 else "?")
    return "".join(out)


def verdict(prefix):
    try:
        vram = open(prefix + ".vram.bin", "rb").read()
    except OSError:
        return None

    if m:
        return "PASS", ""
    m = re.search(r"Failed test (\d+)", txt)
    if m:
        return "FAIL", m.group(1)
    if "Failed" in txt:
        return "FAIL", "?"
    return None, txt.strip()

```
ARM Opcodes: Memory: Block Data Transfer (LDM, STM)
Opcode Format
  Bit    Expl.
  31-28  Condition
  27-25  Must be 100b for this instruction
  24     P - Pre/Post (0=post; add offset after transfer, 1=pre; before trans.)
  23     U - Up/Down Bit (0=down; subtract offset from base, 1=up; add to base)
  22     S - PSR & force user bit (0=No, 1=load PSR or force user mode)
  21     W - Write-back bit (0=no write-back, 1=write address into base)
  20     L - Load/Store bit (0=Store to memory, 1=Load from memory)
          0: STM{cond}{amod} Rn{!},<Rlist>{^}  ;Store (Push)
          1: LDM{cond}{amod} Rn{!},<Rlist>{^}  ;Load  (Pop)
          Whereas, {!}=Write-Back (W), and {^}=PSR/User Mode (S)
  19-16  Rn - Base register                (R0-R14) (not including R15)
  15-0   Rlist - Register List
  (Above 'offset' is meant to be the number of words specified in Rlist.)
Return: No Flags affected.
Execution Time: For normal LDM, nS+1N+1I. For LDM PC, (n+1)S+2N+1I. For STM
(n-1)S+2N. Where n is the number of words transferred.
Addressing Modes {amod}
The IB,IA,DB,DA suffixes directly specify the desired U and P bits:
  IB  increment before          ;P=1, U=1
  IA  increment after           ;P=0, U=1
  DB  decrement before          ;P=1, U=0
  DA  decrement after           ;P=0, U=0
Alternately, FD,ED,FA,EA could be used, mostly to simplify mnemonics for stack
transfers.
  ED  empty stack, descending   ;LDM: P=1, U=1  ;STM: P=0, U=0
  FD  full stack,  descending   ;     P=0, U=1  ;

## [AGENTE]

Trabajo completado y publicado. Resumen honesto de la sesión:

## Lo que se ejecutó y publicó en `main`

| Commit | Contenido |
|---|---|
| `f4763e2` | **Fix de audio nativo Win32**: `waveOutWrite` ya no se llama dentro del callback `WOM_DONE` (prohibido por MSDN) → hilo dedicado + evento. |
| `43e8ab0` | Memoria del repo: fix de audio + nota de desfase de fase de Esmeralda. |
| `e5748bc` | **Suite de regresión `gba-tests`** (`tools/gba_test_suite.py`) con decodificación del veredicto en pantalla. |
| `5068637` | Baseline del suite + verificación de Medabots AX. |
| `6f33c72` | Ignorar `__pycache__`. |

## Verificaciones
- **Builds**: Linux (`make`) y Win32 x64/i686 (`Makefile.win32`) compilan limpios; el .exe solo importa DLLs nativas (GDI32/USER32/WINMM/D3D9), **cero SDL2**. El D-pad POV ya estaba fusionado en `main` (`a8c709f`).
- **Suite gba-tests**: **PASSED 73 / FAILED 51**. Restauré la infraestructura perdida en el reinicio (clon de `alyosha-tas/gba-tests`, harness, decoder). El decoder estaba mal (comparaba el bitmask en vez de expandir cada bit a byte 0/1 como hace la ROM); corregido — `ppu/hello` decodifica "Hello world!" correctamente.
- **Naturaleza de los 51 fallos**: son **precisión de ciclos/pipeline** (IRQ, DMA, timer, LDM/STM con bit S, POP vacío que verifica timer==22), **no bugs de render**. Es el mismo estado que antes; no hay regresión nueva.

## Pendientes reales (no resueltos, honestamente)
1. **Medabots AX (Rokusho)**: extraje la ROM del zip y comparé a f300 → **OAM y EWRAM idénticos a mGBA (0.00%)**; VRAM/pal/IWRAM difieren 1-3% por desfase de fase de carga. La intro renderiza bien. No reproduje un glitch de gameplay porque mGBA segfaultea de forma intermitente en esta ROM (harness inestable).
2. **Precisión de ciclos**: los 51 fallos del suite son el siguiente bloque de trabajo real (empezando por `irq/*` y `DMA/*`, que afectan sincronía en juegos reales), no el render.

Tavily quedó sin cuota; usé GBATEK descargado (`problemkaputt.de/gbatek.htm`) como referencia para el comportamiento de LDM/STM con bit S.

void arm_execute(GBA *g, uint32_t max_cycles) {
    uint32_t start = g->cycle;
    while (g->cycle - start < max_cycles) {
        /* SWI 04h/05h (IntrWait/VBlankIntrWait): only the awaited IRQ releases
           the halt.  Unrelated IRQs are ignored by the BIOS wait loop, so the
           game handler must not run while we are waiting (GBATEK SWI 04h/05h). */
        if (g->cst.halt && g->cst.wait_mask) {

                g->cst.wait_mask = 0;
                g->cst.halt = false;
                /* Leave the awaited flag set: the game's own IRQ/VBlank
                   handler (running after the SWI returns) clears it. */
                (void)done;

void flash_write(GBA *g, uint32_t addr, uint8_t val) {
    Flash *f = &g->flash;
    uint32_t off = addr & 0xFFFF;

    switch (f->state) {
    case FLASH_READY:
        /* A latched command consumes the NEXT write, whatever its address

        if (f->command == FLASH_CMD_PROGRAM) {
            g->save_mem[f->bank * 0x10000u + off] &= val;

cb1ea1a v1.4.8: correcciones de fidelidad GBATEK
9faa4bc feat: BIOS decompression SWIs (LZ77/RLE/Huffman/BitUnPack/filters) + parallel flash
=== full commit ===
9faa4bcd63698cd0f18cb463b1752ca9197dbfbb feat: BIOS decompression SWIs (LZ77/RLE/Huffman/BitUnPack/filters) + parallel flash
Pokemon Emerald stayed on a black screen after the BIOS logo even once the
BIOS handed off to the cartridge. Measuring our core against the mGBA
reference showed the game never left DISPCNT=0000: the BIOS decompression
SWIs were unimplemented, so the LZ77UnCompVram call (SWI 0x12) that unpacks
the whole graphics set wrote nothing and VRAM stayed empty.

Implement BitUnPack (0x10), LZ77 / LZ77UnCompVram (0x11/0x12), Huffman
(0x13), RLE (0x14/0x15) and the difference filters (0x16/0x17/0x18), with
the 3-byte length header and the decompressed length returned in r0. The
VRAM variants advance the destination two bytes per output byte and write
16-bit halfwords.

With the decompressors in place the intro runs: DISPCNT walks
0000 -> 0080 -> 1002 -> 9802 -> 0140 -> 1F40 and the framebuffer tracks the
reference (f1900 nz=251, f2000+ nz=4800, f3000 nz=38400) instead of
freezing blank.

Also add the parallel flash backup chip (JEDEC autoselect, byte program,
sector / chip erase, bank switch) that Emerald probes while initialising
its save, and register it in both Makefiles. Bump to v1.4.7.
```

Byte' the read back of [E00xxxxh] returns the written byte (wait until

after programming.

Two ARM7TDMI/GBATEK fidelity fixes, both documented by the gba-tests psr and
arm suites:
- GBATEK (CPSR/SPSR): \"Only the SPSR of the current mode can be accessed; In
  User and System modes no SPSR exists.\" MRS from SPSR in User/System now
  returns the CPSR, and MSR to SPSR is ignored there instead of writing a
  bogus bank.

  MSR CPSR_c with 0x03 lands in Supervisor (psr test 004). A value of 0 is
  left untouched because that is the boot/system mode and must stay
  privileged (arm psr_transfer test 252).

static uint32_t user_reg(GBA *g, int k) {
    if (bank_of(get_cpsr(g)) != BANK_USR && k >= 8 && k <= 14)
        return g->cpu.bank[BANK_USR][k - 8];
    return k == 15 ? r15(g) + 12 : g->cpu.r[k];
}
static void set_user_reg(GBA *g, int k, uint32_t v) {
    if (bank_of(get_cpsr(g)) != BANK_USR && k >= 8 && k <= 14) {
        g->cpu.bank[BANK_USR][k - 8] = v;
        return;
    }
    if (k == 15) set_pc(g, v & ~3u);
    else         g->cpu.r[k] = v;
}
```

24     P - Pre/Post (0=post; add offset after transfer, 1=pre; before trans.)
  23     U - Up/Down Bit (0=down; subtract offset from base, 1=up; add to base)
  22     S - PSR & force user bit (0=No, 1=load PSR or force user mode)
  21     W - Write-back bit (0=no write-back, 1=write address into base)
  20     L - Load/Store bit (0=Store to memory, 1=Load from memory)
          0: STM{cond}{amod} Rn{!},<Rlist>{^}  ;Store (Push)
          1: LDM{cond}{amod} Rn{!},<Rlist>{^}  ;Load  (Pop)
          Whereas, {!}=Write-Back (W), and {^}=PSR/User Mode (S)
  19-16  Rn - Base register                (R0-R14) (not including R15)
  15-0   Rlist - Register List
  (Above 'offset' is meant to be the number of words specified in Rlist.)
Return: No Flags affected.
Execution Time: For normal LDM, nS+1N+1I. For LDM PC, (n+1)S+2N+1I. For STM
(n-1)S+2N. Where n is the number of words transferred.

Addressing Modes {amod}
The IB,IA,DB,DA suffixes directly specify the desired U and P bits:
  IB  increment before          ;P=1, U=1
  IA  increment after           ;P=0, U=1
  DB  decrement before          ;P=1, U=0
  DA  decrement after           ;P=0, U=0
Alternately, FD,ED,FA,EA could be used, mostly to simplify mnemonics for stack
transfers.
  ED  empty stack, descending   ;LDM: P=1, U=1  ;STM: P=0, U=0
  FD  full stack,  descending   ;     P=0, U=1  ;     P=1, U=0
  EA  empty stack, ascending    ;     P=1, U=0  ;     P=0, U=1

## 2026-10: audio nativo Win32 - waveOutWrite fuera del callback

- `wave_proc` (WOM_DONE) llamaba `waveOutWrite` dentro del propio callback. MSDN
  prohibe invocar cualquier funcion waveOut desde un callback; varios drivers
  corrompen el stream -> el tipico crujido/distorsion del audio nativo.
- Arreglo: el callback solo hace `SetEvent(done)` (evento auto-reset); un hilo
  dedicado mezcla el siguiente fragmento y lo reencola. `audio_close` para el hilo
  antes de `waveOutReset` para que el drain no compita con el reencolado.

## 2026-10: Esmeralda - el diff de la transicion es desfase, no render

- Con VRAM/paleta/registros identicos, el diff de f190+ es fase: contenido identico
  al alinear con delta +1..+2, y va creciendo hasta ~15 frames (mGBA congela la
  pantalla de carga mientras nosotros avanzamos). Confirma la regla de fase anterior.

## 2026-10: suite de regresion gba-tests (baseline 73/133)

- `tools/gba_test_suite.py` ejecuta alyosha-tas/gba-tests contra el harness headless
  y decodifica el veredicto en pantalla. El ROM expande cada bit de glifo a un byte
  0/1 en VRAM (modo 4 BG2); el decoder debe replicar eso, no comparar el bitmask.
- Baseline actual: PASSED 73 / FAILED 51. Los fallos NO son de render: son precision
  de ciclos/pipeline (IRQ, DMA, timer, LDM/STM con S, POP vacio). Mismo estado que
  antes; el suite solo aporta visibilidad, no una regresion nueva.
- `ppu/hello` decodifica "Hello world!" -> el decoder es correcto.

  `[E00xxxxh]=dat`), y tras *Erase* devuelve FFh. El codigo anterior devolvia el
  byte con el **bit 7 invertido durante 64 lecturas** tras cada program/erase

## 2026-10: ARM7TDMI SPSR y bit 4 del campo modo (psr 001 -> 008)

- GBATEK (CPSR/SPSR): *"Only the SPSR of the current mode can be accessed; In
  User and System modes no SPSR exists."* `MRS SPSR` en User/System devuelve el
  CPSR; `MSR SPSR` se ignora (`has_spsr()` en `arm.c`).
- El bit 4 del campo modo se lee siempre como 1 para las codificaciones
  invalidas `0xxnnb`: `MSR cpsr_c, 0x03` cae en Supervisor (psr test 004). Un
  valor de modo 0 se deja intacto (es el modo de arranque y debe seguir siendo
  privilegiado, arm `psr_transfer` test 252). `change_mode()` fuerza `|= 0x10`
  solo si el modo != 0.
- `psr/psr` pasa de fallar en 001 a 008 (lo restante es timing de ciclos).
  Baseline del suite se mantiene en 75.

"""Compare our core framebuffer (RGB555 screen.bin) against mGBA PPM.

/* Run one video frame: step the PPU line by line, running the CPU for the
 * cycles each scanline takes, firing HBlank/VBlank/VCount interrupts. */
static void run_frame_core(GBA *g) {
    const uint32_t visible_cycles = 960;     /* 240 px * 4 ciclos */
    const uint32_t hblank_cycles  = 272;     /* total 1232 por linea */

    ppu_frame_start(g);                      /* recarga puntos de referencia afines */
    apu_step(g, 0);

    for (int line = 0; line < 228; line++) {

example, when using a 64 kHz sample rate, 16 bytes of sound DMA data are

with higher priority should not be operated for longer than 0.25ms. (This
problem does not arise for HBlank transfers as HBlank time is limited to
16.212us.)

Game Pak DMA
Only DMA 3 may be used to transfer data to/from Game Pak ROM or Flash ROM - it
cannot access Game Pak SRAM though (as SRAM data bus is limited to 8bit units).
In normal mode, DMA is requested as long until Word Count becomes zero. When
setting the 'Game Pack DRQ' bit, then the cartridge must contain an external
circuit which outputs a /DREQ signal. Note that there is only one pin for /DREQ
and /IREQ, thus the cartridge may not supply /IREQs while using DRQ mode.

Video Capture Mode (DMA3 only)
Intended to copy a bitmap from memory (or from external hardware/camera) to
VRAM. When using this transfer mode, set the repeat bit, and write the number
of data units (per scanline) to the word count register. Capture works similar
like HBlank DMA, however, the transfer is started when VCOUNT=2, it is then
repeated each scanline, and it gets stopped when VCOUNT=162.

static int32_t sext28(uint32_t v) { return (int32_t)(v << 4) >> 4; }

/* Access cost of one DMA data unit, in GBA clock cycles, per GBATEK
 * "GBA DMA Transfers / Transfer Rate/Timing": the transfer time for n units is
 *   2N + 2(n-1)S + xI
 * where N/S are the non-sequential/sequential costs of the *slower* of the two
 * buses and each unit on a 16-bit bus costs two accesses (GBATEK "GamePak uses
 * 16bit data bus, so that a 32bit access is split into TWO 16bit accesses").
 * Waitstates come from WAITCNT; internal memory runs at 1 cycle per access.
 */
static int dma_unit_cycles(GBA *g, uint32_t src, uint32_t dst, int word) {
    uint16_t wc = (uint16_t)(g->io[0x204] | (g->io[0x205] << 8));
    int n, s;
    if ((src | dst) & 0x0E000000u) {          /* GamePak ROM (WS0) / ROM mirror */
        n = 5 - (wc & 3);                     /* 0..3 -> 5,4,3,2 cycles */
        s = (wc & 0x10) ? 2 : 5;              /* 0 -> 5 cycles, 1 -> 2 cycles */
    } else if ((src | dst) & 0x02000000u) {   /* EWRAM: 2 waitstates (4000800h default 0Dh) */
        n = s = 3;
    } else {                                  /* IWRAM/VRAM/palette/OAM/IO/BIOS */
        n = s = 1;
    }
    if (word) {                               /* 32-bit unit -> two 16-bit accesses */
        int second = (n + s) > 2 * s ? n : s; /* non-seq first, then sequential */
        return n + second;
    }
    return s;
}

        return (uint16_t)(g->io[reg] | (g->io[reg+1] << 8));
    }
}

void dma_trigger(GBA *g, int timing) {
    for (int ch = 0; ch < 4; ch++) {
        DmaChan *d = &g->dma[ch];
        if (d->enabled && d->timing == timing) dma_run(g, ch);
    }
}

/* El FIFO A/B pide datos (<= 16 bytes en cola): dispara el DMA1/DMA2 cuyo destino sea el FIFO. */
void dma_fifo_request(GBA *g, int fifo) {
    uint32_t target = fifo ? 0x040000A4u : 0x040000A0u;
    for (int ch = 1; ch <= 2; ch++) {
        DmaChan *d = &g->dma[ch];
        if (d->enabled && d->timing == 3 && (d->dst & 0x0FFFFFFFu) == target) {
            dma_run(g, ch);
            return;
        }
    }
}

static void timer_overflow(GBA *g, int i, uint32_t n) {
    Timer *t = &g->timer[i];
    if (t->irq_enable) g->if_reg |= (uint16_t)(IF_TIMER0 << i);
    if (i < 2) apu_timer_overflow(g, i, n);          /* reloj de los FIFOs de Direct Sound */

        if (nt->enabled && nt->count_up) timer_add(g, i + 1, n);
    }
}

static void timer_add(GBA *g, int i, uint32_t ticks) {
    Timer *t = &g->timer[i];
    uint32_t cnt = (uint32_t)t->counter + ticks;
    if (cnt <= 0xFFFF) { t->counter = (uint16_t)cnt; return; }
    uint32_t period = 0x10000u - t->reload;          /* 1 .. 0x10000 */
    uint32_t over = cnt - 0x10000u;
    uint32_t n = 1 + over / period;                  /* desbordamientos en este paso */
    t->counter = (uint16_t)(t->reload + over % period);
    timer_overflow(g, i, n);
}

The ARM CPU provides two interrupt sources, IRQ and FIQ. In the GBA only IRQ is
used. In normal GBAs, the FIQ signal is shortcut to VDD35, ie. the signal is
always high, and there is no way to generate a FIQ by hardware. The registers
R8..12_fiq could be used by software (when switching into FIQ mode by writing
to CPSR) - however, this might make the game incompatible with hardware
debuggers (which are reportedly using FIQs for debugging purposes).

GBA System Control
------------------

4000204h - WAITCNT - Waitstate Control (R/W)
This register is used to configure game pak access timings. The game pak ROM is
mirrored to three address regions at 08000000h, 0A000000h, and 0C000000h, these
areas are called Wait State 0-2. Different access timings may be assigned to
each area (this might be useful in case that a game pak contains several ROM
chips with different access times each).
  Bit   Expl.
  0-1   SRAM Wait Control          (0..3 = 4,3,2,8 cycles)
  2-3   Wait State 0 First Access  (0..3 = 4,3,2,8 cycles)
  4     Wait State 0 Second Access (0..1 = 2,1 cycles)
  5-6   Wait State 1 First Access  (0..3 = 4,3,2,8 cycles)
  7     Wait State 1 Second Access (0..1 = 4,1 cycles; unlike above WS0)
  8-9   Wait State 2 First Access  (0..3 = 4,3,2,8 cycles)
  10    Wait State 2 Second Access (0..1 = 8,1 cycles; unlike above WS0,WS1)
  11-12 PHI Terminal Output        (0..3 = Disable, 4.19MHz, 8.38MHz, 16.78MHz)
  13    Not used
```

124:void apu_timer_overflow(GBA *g, int timer, uint32_t n) {
void apu_timer_overflow(GBA *g, int timer, uint32_t n) {
    Apu *a = &g->apu;
    for (int f = 0; f < 2; f++) {
        int sel = (a->cnt_h >> (f ? 14 : 10)) & 1;
        if (sel != timer) continue;
        for (uint32_t k = 0; k < n; k++) {
            if (a->fifo_len[f] > 0) {
                a->fifo_held[f] = a->fifo[f][a->fifo_head[f]];
                a->fifo_head[f] = (a->fifo_head[f] + 1) & 31;
                a->fifo_len[f]--;
            }
            if (a->fifo_len[f] <= 16) dma_fifo_request(g, f);
        }
    }
}

/* ---------------------------------------------------------------- registros */
static uint16_t ch_lenflag(const Apu *a, int i) {
    switch (i) {
    case 0: return a->r1x & 0x4000;
    case 1: return a->r2h & 0x4000;
    case 2: return a->r3x & 0x4000;
    default: return a->r4h & 0x4000;
    }
}

# Makefile.win32 - cross-compile the native Windows build (no SDL).
#
# The Windows build links directly to GDI / Direct3D 9 / waveOut (WinMM);
# SDL2 is intentionally not used. Build from Linux with a MinGW cross
# toolchain, or from Windows with MinGW-w64:
#
#   make -f Makefile.win32                     # x86_64, mingw64
#   make -f Makefile.win32 ARCH=i686           # i686, mingw32
#
# Variables:
#   CROSS  toolchain prefix (default: x86_64-w64-mingw32- / i686-w64-mingw32-)

ARCH ?= x86_64
ifeq ($(ARCH),i686)
  CROSS ?= i686-w64-mingw32-
else
  CROSS ?= x86_64-w64-mingw32-
endif

CC      = $(CROSS)gcc
RC      = $(CROSS)windres
CFLAGS  = -std=c99 -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Isrc -D_WIN32
LDFLAGS = -mwindows
LDLIBS  = -lwinmm -ld3d9 -lgdi32 -luser32 -lcomdlg32 -lm

SRC = src/gba.c src/mem.c src/arm.c src/ppu.c src/apu.c src/bios.c \
      src/fb.c src/video.c src/gui.c src/eeprom.c src/flash.c src/win32.c

# Object files live in a per-architecture directory: x86_64 and i686 builds
# share src/ but their objects are not interchangeable.
OBJDIR = build/$(ARCH)
OBJ = $(patsubst src/%.c,$(OBJDIR)/%.o,$(SRC)) $(OBJDIR)/icon.res

TARGET = boycottadvance-reborn-$(ARCH).exe

all: $(TARGET)

$(TARGET): $(OBJ)
        $(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(LDFLAGS) $(OBJ) $(LDLIBS) -o $@

$(OBJDIR)/icon.res: src/icon.rc assets/icon.ico | $(OBJDIR)
        $(RC) -O coff -i $< -o $@

$(OBJDIR)/%.o: src/%.c | $(OBJDIR)
        $(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $@

$(OBJDIR):
        mkdir -p $(OBJDIR)

clean:
        rm -rf

* DMA engine (GBATEK: GBA DMA Transfers)
 * ========================================================================= */
void dma_run(GBA *g, int ch) {
    DmaChan *d = &g->dma[ch];
    if (!d->enabled) return;

    /* Timing 3 en DMA1/2 = modo FIFO de sonido: siempre 4 palabras de 32 bit,
       destino fijo, el contador DMAxCNT_L se ignora. */
    bool fifo = (d->timing == 3) && (ch == 1 || ch == 2);
    uint32_t unit = (d->word || fifo) ? 4 : 2;
    uint32_t count;
    if (fifo) count = 4;
    else if (ch == 3) { count = d->count & 0xFFFF; if (!count) count = 0x10000; }
    else              { count = d->count & 0x3FFF; if (!count) count = 0x4000; }

    uint32_t src = d->src & ~(unit - 1);
    uint32_t dst = d->dst & ~(unit - 1);

    /* EEPROM es bit-serie y solo accesible por DMA de 16 bit: el recuento le dice

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Run the alyosha-tas/gba-tests suite against the headless harness.

Each ROM renders its verdict as mode-4 BG2 text; the harness dumps VRAM and the
verdict is decoded from the 8x8 glyphs in lib/glyphs.asm (the ROM expands each
glyph bit to one 0/1 byte per pixel).

Env:
  SUITE_ROOT  gba-tests checkout      (default /tmp/gba-tests)
  HH          headless harness binary (default /tmp/hh)
  BIOS        GBA BIOS image          (default <repo>/gba_bios.bin)
  FRAMES      frames per ROM          (default 400)
  OUT         scratch dump directory  (default /tmp/gba-suite-out)
"""
import glob
import os
import re

/* mGBA comparison harness: load ROM, run N frames, dump framebuffer (PPM),
 * audio IO, and V/O memory.
 *
 * Compile with the same -D macros the lib was built with so struct mCore matches:
 *   gcc -std=c11 -DENABLE_DEBUGGERS -DENABLE_DIRECTORIES -DENABLE_VFS \
 *       -D_GNU_SOURCE -I/workspace/mgba/include tools/mgbaharness.c \
 *       -L/workspace/mgba/build -lmgba -lm
 *
 * Usage:
 *   mgbaharness <rom> <frames> [audio.pcm] [frame.ppm]
 * Env:
 *   FASTBOOT=1  : write forced-blank + VBlank IRQ to mimic our fastboot boot
 *   DUMPDIR=<d> : dump vram.bin / pal.bin / oam.bin through the CPU bus
 */
#include <mgba/core/core.h>
#include <mgba/gba/core.h>
#include <mgba/core/interface.h>
#include <mgba/core/config.h>
#include <mgba-util/audio-buffer.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <fcntl.h>
#include <mgba-util/vfs.h>

int main(int argc, char** argv) {
    if (argc < 3) { fprintf(stderr, "usage: %s <rom> <frames> [audio.pcm] [frame.ppm]\n", argv[0]); return 2; }
    const char* rom = argv[1];
    int nframes = atoi(argv[2]);
```

static void timer_add(GBA *g, int i, uint32_t ticks) {
    Timer *t = &g->timer[i];
    uint32_t cnt = (uint32_t)t->counter + ticks;
    if (cnt <= 0xFFFF) { t->counter = (uint16_t)cnt; return; }
    uint32_t period = 0x10000u - t->reload;          /* 1 .. 0x10000 */
    uint32_t over = cnt - 0x10000u;
    uint32_t n = 1 + over / period;                  /* desbordamientos en este paso */
    t->counter = (uint16_t)(t->reload + over % period);
    timer_overflow(g, i, n);
}

void io_update_timers(GBA *g, uint32_t cycles) {
    for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++) {
        Timer *t = &g->timer[i];
        if (!t->enabled) continue;
        if (i > 0 && t->count_up) continue;          /* avanza solo por cascada */
        uint32_t ps = t->prescaler ? (uint32_t)t->prescaler : 1u;
        t->clock += cycles;                          /* acumulador: no se pierde el resto */
        uint32_t ticks = t->clock / ps;
        t->clock -= ticks * ps;
        if (ticks) timer_add(g, i, ticks);
    }
}

       2N+2(n-1)S+xI cycles. Timers keep counting while the DMA holds the bus,
       so those cycles are charged to the timers that were already running when
       the transfer began (a DMA that itself enables a timer must not bill it). */

        else           gba_write16(g, dst, gba_read16(g, src));
        /* src: 0 incrementa, 1 decrementa, 2 fijo, 3 prohibido (se trata como incremento) */
        if (d->src_ctl == 1) src -= unit;
        else if (d->src_ctl != 2) src += unit;
        /* dst: 0 incrementa, 1 decrementa, 2 fijo, 3 incrementa + recarga al repetir */
        if (!fifo) {
            if (d->dst_ctl == 1) dst -= unit;
            else if (d->dst_ctl != 2) dst += unit;
        }
    }

    d->dst = dst;
    gba_add_cycles(g, dma_cyc);

    The Windows port no longer links SDL2 at all. It uses only the native
    APIs the original BoycottAdvance used:
      - window + menu bar (GDI, full Win32 menu via gui.c)
      - frame presentation: GDI blit (StretchDIBits) or Direct3D 9
      - audio: waveOut (WinMM) driving apu_mix
      - input: GetAsyncKeyState + WinMM joystick (ctl_joy_poll, POV hat)
      - file dialogs / message boxes: commdlg / user32

    Refactors:
      - video.h/video.c: vid_init takes void* (HWND on Windows,
        SDL_Window elsewhere). SDL backends are #ifndef _WIN32 only;
        Windows exposes GDI and D3D9.
      - vk.c: vk_create takes void* (SDL_Window cast internally).
      - gui.c/gui.h: joystick layer (WinMM joyGetPosEx with 45-degree POV
        hats) plus native-only Frame Buffer submenu on Windows.
      - main.c: remains the non-Windows SDL frontend; Makefile selects
        win32.c for native Windows builds.
      - new src/win32.c: WinMain, WndProc, waveOut audio, frame loop with
        throttle/FPS, INI persistence, key capture, savestates, screenshot.

    Builds verified: Linux (SDL), Windows x86_64 and i686 (mingw, no SDL).

# Makefile.win32 - cross-compile the native Windows build (no SDL).
#
# The Windows build links directly to GDI / Direct3D 9 / waveOut (WinMM);
# SDL2 is intentionally not used. Build from Linux with a MinGW cross
# toolchain, or from Windows with MinGW-w64:
#
#   make -f Makefile.win32                     # x86_64, mingw64
#   make -f Makefile.win32 ARCH=i686           # i686, mingw32
#
# Variables:
#   CROSS  toolchain prefix (default: x86_64-w64-mingw32- / i686-w64-mingw32-)

ARCH ?= x86_64
ifeq ($(ARCH),i686)
  CROSS ?= i686-w64-mingw32-
else
  CROSS ?= x86_64-w64-mingw32-
endif

CC      = $(CROSS)gcc
RC      = $(CROSS)windres
CFLAGS  = -std=c99 -O2 -Wall -Wextra -Isrc -D_WIN32
LDFLAGS = -mwindows
LDLIBS  = -lwinmm -ld3d9 -lgdi32 -luser32 -lcomdlg32 -lm

SRC = src/gba.c src/mem.c src/arm.c src/ppu.c src/apu.c src/bios.c \
      src/fb.c src/video.c src/gui.c src/eeprom.c src/flash.c src/win32.c

# Object files live in a per-architecture directory: x86_64 and i686 builds
# share src/ but their objects are not interchangeable.
OBJDIR = build/$(ARCH)
OBJ = $(patsubst src/%.c,$(OBJDIR)/%.o,$(SRC)) $(OBJDIR)/icon.res

TARGET = boycottadvance-reborn-$(ARCH).exe

all: $(TARGET)

$(TARGET): $(OBJ)
        $(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(LDFLAGS) $(OBJ) $(LDLIBS) -o $@

$(OBJDIR)/icon.res: src/icon.rc assets/icon.ico | $(OBJDIR)
        $(RC) -O coff -i $< -o $@

$(OBJDIR)/%.o: src/%.c | $(OBJDIR)
        $(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $@

$(OBJDIR):
        mkdir -p $(OBJDIR)

clean:
        rm -rf 
... [88 caracteres omitidos] ...

## Resumen

**Corregí la premisa inicial**: el commit+push del D-pad y la eliminación de SDL2 **ya estaban hechos y mergeados**. Verifiqué con `git merge-base --is-ancestor` que `a8c709f` (D-pad POV), `22cb833` (eliminación de SDL2) y el hito Win32 nativo están en `origin/main`.

### Trabajo de esta sesión

**1. Commit + push del fix de DMA (pendiente real)**
- Commit `3f7136a` en `main`, pusheado a `origin/main` (`7e87d00..3f7136a`). El token embebido en el remoto había expirado; lo refresqué con `$GITHUB_TOKEN`.
- Contenido: `dma_run()` ahora modela el coste real de bus GBATEK (`2N+2(n-1)S+xI`) con clasificación por región (EWRAM=2, ROM según WS0, internas=0) y **alimenta los timers** con esos ciclos.
- `timing/dma_long`: FAIL 001 → **PASS**.

**2. Hallazgo importante sobre `prefetcher_dma`**
Su "PASS" en el baseline era **espurio**: leía `TM0CNT_L` y obtenía 0 porque los timers solo se actualizaban por scanline, nunca por instrucción. El fix de DMA lo expone (ahora da FAIL 002). Es decir, el suite neto se mantiene en 75: se arregla `dma_long` y se destapa un bug latente.

**3. Validación de no-regresión**
- Pokémon Esmeralda y Fire Emblem: **bit-idénticos** (screen/vram/pal/oam) tras 900 frames frente al baseline.
- Suite completa: 75 PASSED / 49 FAILED / 9 UNKNOWN — idéntico al baseline registrado.

**4. Verificación del hito Win32 sin SDL2**
Reinstalé mingw-w64 y compilé ambos targets con `Makefile.win32`:
- `boycottadvance-reborn-x86_64.exe` y `-i686.exe`: **cero warnings**.
- Importaciones: solo `GDI32, USER32, WINMM, comdlg32, d3d9, SHELL32, msvcrt` — **0 referencias a SDL**.
- Confirmado: video nativo (GDI `StretchDIBits` + D3D9), audio WinMM (`waveOutOpen/Write`), `WndProc` nativa, y árbol de menús completo (File/Window/Options/Help) **sin menú Debug**.

### Pendiente para la próxima sesión
La **causa raíz** del timing de timers: `gba.c` pre-carga los timers en bloques de scanline antes de ejecutar la CPU, así que un timer habilitado a mitad de scanline no ve los ciclos de las instrucciones. Intenté sincronización por instrucción (`io_sync_timers` en `arm_execute`) pero rompe 4 tests porque el resto del modelo de ciclos (`add_cycles` de ARM/Thumb) es aproximado; hay que revisarlos juntos. Todo quedó documentado en `AGENTS.md`.

=== apu_step ===
void apu_step(GBA *g, uint32_t cycles) {
    Apu *a = &g->apu;
    a->sample_acc += (uint64_t)cycles * SAMPLE_RATE;
    while (a->sample_acc >= CPU_HZ) {
        a->sample_acc -= CPU_HZ;
        int16_t l, r;
        gen_sample(a, &l, &r);
        ring_push(l, r);
    }
}
=== apu_timer_overflow ===
/* ---------------------------------------------------------------- FIFOs */
void apu_fifo_write(GBA *g, int ch, const uint8_t *bytes, int nbytes) {
    Apu *a = &g->apu;
    ch = ch ? 1 : 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < nbytes; i++) {
        if (a->fifo_len[ch] >= 32) break;                   /* FIFO lleno */
        a->fifo[ch][(a->fifo_head[ch] + a->fifo_len[ch]) & 31] = (int8_t)bytes[i];
        a->fifo_len[ch]++;
    }
}

/* Un timer desbordo n veces: los FIFOs que lo usan sacan n muestras. */
void apu_timer_overflow(GBA *g, int timer, uint32_t n) {
    Apu *a = &g->apu;
    for (int f = 0; f < 2; f++) {
        int sel = (a->cnt_h >> (f ? 14 : 10)) & 1;
        if (sel != timer) continue;
        for (uint32_t k = 0; k < n; k++) {
            if (a->fifo_len[f] > 0) {
                a->fifo_held[f] = a->fifo[f][a->fifo_head[f]];
                a->fifo_head[f] = (a->fifo_head[f] + 1) & 31;
                a->fifo_len[f]--;
            }
            if (a->fifo_len[f] <= 16) dma_fifo_request(g, f);
        }
    }
}

void dma_trigger(GBA *g, int timing) {
    for (int ch = 0; ch < 4; ch++) {
        DmaChan *d = &g->dma[ch];
        if (d->enabled && d->timing == timing) dma_run(g, ch);
    }
}

/* El FIFO A/B pide datos (<= 16 bytes en cola): dispara el DMA1/DMA2 cuyo destino sea el FIFO. */
void dma_fifo_request(GBA *g, int fifo) {
    uint32_t target = fifo ? 0x040000A4u : 0x040000A0u;
    for (int ch = 1; ch <= 2; ch++) {
        DmaChan *d = &g->dma[ch];
        if (d->enabled && d->timing == 3 && (d->dst & 0x0FFFFFFFu) == target) {
            dma_run(g, ch);
            return;
        }
    }
}

    for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++) {
        Timer *t = &g->timer[i];
        if (!t->enabled) continue;

        uint32_t ps = t->prescaler ? (uint32_t)t->prescaler : 1u;

        uint32_t ticks = t->clock / ps;
        t->clock -= ticks * ps;
        if (ticks) timer_add(g, i, ticks);
    }
}

/*
 * arm.c - ARM7TDMI interpreter (ARM + Thumb) for BoycottAdvance Reborn.
 *
 * Revisado contra GBATEK ("ARM CPU Instruction Set", "THUMB Instruction Set",
 * "ARM CPU Exceptions", "ARM Pseudo Instructions and Directives").
 *
 * Correcciones respecto a v1.4.7 (ver AUDITORIA_GBATEK.md):
 *  - SWI en modo ARM (bits 27-24 = 1111) nunca se ejecutaba.
 *  - Entrada IRQ en Thumb guardaba LR = PC+2 (debe ser siempre PC+4).
 *  - LDR/LDRH/LDRSH desalineados (rotacion), SWP/SWPB, flags de UMULL/SMULL.
 *  - STM con writeback si Rn esta en la lista, lista vacia, base en la lista.
 *  - Thumb formato 8 (STRH/LDSB/LDRH/LDSH) estaba mal decodificado.
 *  - Thumb ROR por registro con cuenta 0, BX Thumb->ARM (alineacion), LDMIA con Rb en lista.
 *  - Condicion NV (0xF) = nunca; ROR por registro multiplo de 32.
 */
#include "gba.h"
#include "arm.h"
#include "mem.h"
#include <stdio.h>

static inline bool thumb_mode(GBA *g) { return (g->cpu.cpsr & CPSR_T) != 0; }

/* r15 holds PC of the currently executed instruction. Reads of r15 add the
 * classic ARM pipeline offset (+8 ARM / +4 Thumb); writes clear bit 0. */
static inline uint32_t read_reg(GBA *g, int n) {
    if (n == 15) return g->cpu.r[15] + (thumb_mode(g) ? 4 : 8);
    return g->cpu.r[n];
}
static inline void write_reg(GBA *g, int n, uint32_t v) {
    if (n == 15) v &= ~1u;
    g->cpu.r[n] = v;
}
static inline uint32_t r15(GBA *g) { return g->cpu.r[15]; }
static inline void set_pc(GBA *g, uint32_t v) { g->cpu.r[15] = v & ~1u; }

Eventually, data fetches can take place parallel with opcode fetches.

 That is NOT true for LDM (works only for LDR/LDRB/LDRH).
 That is NOT true for DATA in SAME memory region than CODE.
 That is NOT true for DATA in ITCM (no matter if CODE is in ITCM).

*********************

NDS9 Busses
Unlike ARM7, the ARM9 has separate code and data busses, allowing it to perform
code and data fetches simultaneously (provided that both are in different
memory regions).
Normally, opcode execution times are calculated as "(codetime+datatime)", with
the two busses, it can (ideally) be "MAX(codetime,datatime)", so the data
access time may virtually take "NULL" clock cycles.
In practice, DTCM and Data Cache access can take NULL cycles (however, data
access to ITCM can't).
When executing code in cache/itcm, data access to non-cache/tcm won't be any
faster than with only one bus (as it's best, it could subtract 0.5 cycles from
datatime, but, the access must be "aligned" to the bus-clock, so the
"datatime-0.5" will be rounded back to the original "datatime").
When executing code in uncached main ram, and accessing data (elsewhere than in
main memory, cache/tcm), then execution time is typically
"codetime+datatime-2".

NDS9 Internal Cycles
Additionally to codetime+datatime, some opcodes include one or more internal

different on ARM9. First of, on the NDS9, the internal cycles are of course

Above 'trap' is meant to be the execution time for exceptions. And '{cond}

The separate meaning of the N,S,I,C cycles is:

N - Non-sequential cycle
Requests a transfer to/from an address which is NOT related to the address used
in the previous cycle. (Called 1st Access in GBA language).
The execution time for 1N is 1 clock cycle (plus non-sequential access
waitstates).

S - Sequential cycle
Requests a transfer to/from an address which is located directly after the
address used in the previous cycle. Ie. for 16bit or 32bit accesses at
incrementing addresses, the first access is Non-sequential, the following
accesses are sequential. (Called 2nd Access in GBA language).
The execution time for 1S is 1 clock cycle (plus sequential access waitstates).

I - Internal Cycle
CPU is just too busy, not even requesting a memory transfer for now.
The execution time for 1I is 1 clock cycle (without any waitstates).

C - Coprocessor Cycle
The CPU uses the data bus to communicate with the coprocessor (if any), but no
memory transfers are requested.

Memory Waitstates
Ideally, memory may be accessed free of waitstates (1N and 1S are then equal to
1 clock cycle each). However, a memory s

# BoycottAdvance-Reborn â€” notas de depuraciĂłn

ReimplementaciĂłn limpia del emulador GBA BoycottAdvance 0.2.8 (C).

registros LCD/sonido/DMA/timers/interrupciones, opcodes ARM/THUMB, funciones BIOS.

navegador; no usar `curl` para leerlo.

void ARMRaiseIRQ(struct ARMCore* cpu) {
        if (cpu->cpsr.i) {
                return;
        }
        union PSR cpsr = cpu->cpsr;
        int instructionWidth;
        if (cpu->executionMode == MODE_THUMB) {
                instructionWidth = WORD_SIZE_THUMB;
        } else {
                instructionWidth = WORD_SIZE_ARM;
        }
        ARMSetPrivilegeMode(cpu, MODE_IRQ);
        cpu->cpsr.priv = MODE_IRQ;
        cpu->gprs[ARM_LR] = cpu->gprs[ARM_PC] - instructionWidth + WORD_SIZE_ARM;
        cpu->gprs[ARM_PC] = BASE_IRQ;
        _ARMSetMode(cpu, MODE_ARM);
        cpu->cycles += ARMWritePC(cpu);
        cpu->spsr = cpsr;
        cpu->cpsr.i = 1;
        cpu->halted = 0;
}

/* Tras restaurar el CPSR desde SPSR el PC debe alinearse segun el estado resultante. */
/* User-bank view of a register, for LDM/STM with the S bit and no PC in the
 * list: the transfer uses the User mode registers, not the current bank
 * (GBATEK "ARM Block Data Transfer"; gba-tests #511/#512). */
static uint32_t user_reg(GBA *g, int k) {
    if (bank_of(get_cpsr(g)) != BANK_USR && k >= 8 && k <= 14)
        return g->cpu.bank[BANK_USR][k - 8];
    return k == 15 ? r15(g) + 12 : g->cpu.r[k];
}
static void set_user_reg(GBA *g, int k, uint32_t v) {
    if (bank_of(get_cpsr(g)) != BANK_USR && k >= 8 && k <= 14) {
        g->cpu.bank[BANK_USR][k - 8] = v;
        return;
    }
    if (k == 15) set_pc(g, v & ~3u);
    else         g->cpu.r[k] = v;
}

static void branch_restore(GBA *g, uint32_t target) {
    set_pc(g, target & (thumb_mode(g) ? ~1u : ~3u));
}

- Medabots AX: nuestra f600 == mGBA f606.
  - En Esmeralda, mGBA congela la pantalla de f744 a f760 y luego se recupera;
    nosotros arrancamos el cambio en f749. No es un bug nuestro: es la misma
    transicion de carga reproducida a distinta velocidad (DMA/BIOS).
- **Ambos reconvergen**: Medabots AX da 0.00% exacto en f300-f410 y en f460-f570;
  Esmeralda 0.00% en f680-f748. Por tanto un diff grande en un frame concreto NO
  implica un bug de render: hay que buscar el frame equivalente del otro emulador.
- **Regla practica**: antes de perseguir un diff, comparar nuestra fN contra mGBA
  f(N-k) para k en un rango (p.ej. 0..30) y quedarse con el minimo. Si el minimo es
  ~0, es desfase de fase, no divergencia funcional.
- **Correccion de un diagnostico previo**: el supuesto "byte-swap de OAM bytes 6/7"
  (nosotros `00 66` vs mGBA `66 00`) era un artefacto de comparar contra un frame
  de mGBA congelado/obsoleto. La ruta de escritura de OAM en `src/mem.c` es
  little-endian correcta (`wr16_al`/`wr32_al`, 8-bit ignorado en case 0x07).

SRC = src/gba.c src/mem.c src/arm.c src/ppu.c src/apu.c src/bios.c src/fb.c src/video.c src/gui.c src/eeprom.c src/flash.c

ifneq ($(OS),Windows_NT)
  CFLAGS += $(shell pkg-config --cflags sdl2)
  LDLIBS += $(shell pkg-config --libs sdl2)
  SRC += src/main.c
  VK_LIBS = $(shell pkg-config --libs vulkan 2>/dev/null)
  ifneq ($(VK_LIBS),)
    CFLAGS += -DHAVE_VULKAN $(shell pkg-config --cflags vulkan 2>/dev/null)
    LDLIBS += $(VK_LIBS)
    SRC += src/vk.c
  endif
else
  RC ?= windres
  ICON_OBJ = src/icon.res
  SRC += src/win32.c
  LDLIBS += -lwinmm -ld3d9 -lgdi32 -luser32 -lcomdlg32
endif
OBJ = $(SRC:.c=.o) $(ICON_OBJ)

all: boycottadvance-reborn

boycottadvance-reborn: $(OBJ)
        $(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(OBJ) $(LDLIBS) -o $@

src/icon.res: src/icon.rc assets/icon.ico
```

void arm_execute(GBA *g, uint32_t max_cycles) {
    uint32_t start = g->cycle;
    while (g->cycle - start < max_cycles) {
        /* SWI 04h/05h (IntrWait/VBlankIntrWait): only the awaited IRQ releases
           the halt.  Unrelated IRQs are ignored by the BIOS wait loop, so the
           game handler must not run while we are waiting (GBATEK SWI 04h/05h). */
        if (g->cst.halt && g->cst.wait_mask) {
            if (g->if_reg & g->cst.wait_mask) {

                g->cst.halt = false;

/* Run one video frame: step the PPU line by line, running the CPU for the
 * cycles each scanline takes, firing HBlank/VBlank/VCount interrupts. */
static void run_frame_core(GBA *g) {
    const uint32_t visible_cycles = 960;     /* 240 px * 4 ciclos */
    const uint32_t hblank_cycles  = 272;     /* total 1232 por linea */

    apu_step(g, 0);

        int vm = (g->ppu.dispstat >> 8) & 0xFF;
        g->ppu.vcount = (uint16_t)line;

        /* DISPSTAT bits 0-1: bit0 VBlank (lineas 160-226), bit1 HBlank en la
           parte no visible; bit2 VCount match.  Bit1 lo mantiene el nucleo. */
        uint16_t st = (uint16_t)(g->ppu.dispstat & 0xFFF8);
        if (line >= 160 && line <= 226) st |= 0x0001;        /* VBlank (160..226, no 227) */
        if (line == vm)  st |= 0x0004;                      /* VCount match */
        g->ppu.dispstat = st;

        /* VBlank: la IRQ se dispara en la linea 159, un scanline antes de que

        if (line == 159) {
            if (g->ppu.dispstat & 0x0008) g->if_reg |= IF_VBLANK;

4000004h - DISPSTAT - General LCD Status (Read/Write)
Display status and Interrupt control. The H-Blank conditions are generated once
per scanline, including for the 'hidden' scanlines during V-Blank.

  Bit   Expl.
  0     V-Blank flag   (Read only) (1=VBlank) (set in line 160..226; not 227)
  1     H-Blank flag   (Read only) (1=HBlank) (toggled in all lines, 0..227)
  2     V-Counter flag (Read only) (1=Match)  (set in selected line)     (R)
  3     V-Blank IRQ Enable         (1=Enable)                          (R/W)
  4     H-Blank IRQ Enable         (1=Enable)                          (R/W)
  5     V-Counter IRQ Enable       (1=Enable)                          (R/W)
  6     Not used (0) / DSi: LCD Initialization Ready (0=Busy, 1=Ready)   (R)
  7     Not used (0) / NDS: MSB of V-Vcount Setting (LYC.Bit8) (0..262)(R/W)
  8-15  V-Count Setting (LYC)      (0..227)                            (R/W)

The V-Count-Setting value is much the same as LYC of older gameboys, when its
value is identical to the content of the VCOUNT register then the V-Counter
flag is set (Bit 2), and (if enabled in Bit 5) an interrupt is requested.
Although the drawing time is only 960 cycles (240*4), the H-Blank flag is "0"
for a total of 1006 cycles.

4000006h - VCOUNT - Vertical Counter (Read only)
Indicates the currently drawn scanline, values in range from 160..227 indicate
'hidden' scanlines within VBlank area.

  Bit   Expl.
  0-7   Current Scanline (LY)      (0..227)

  suite (alyosha-tas) prueba un quirk de hardware que ninguno de los dos
  implementa. No malgastar esfuerzo ahi.

## 2026-10: coste real de bus del DMA (GBATEK 2N+2(n-1)S+xI)

- `dma_run()` cobraba `1 ciclo/32-bit` y `2/16-bit` (constante) al bus y no
  tocaba los timers. GBATEK (GBA DMA Transfers, "Transfer Rate/Timing") define
  `2N + 2(n-1)S + xI`: el `2` es por unidad (no por acceso), `N/S` son los
  waitstates non-sequential/sequential de la region, y el `I` es el ciclo
  interno del bus de 16 bit que obliga a partir un acceso de 32 bit en dos.
- Implementado en `src/mem.c`: `dma_region()` clasifica por direccion
  (BIOS/IWRAM/IO/PAL/VRAM/OAM sin waitstates, EWRAM=2 en reset, ROM segun WS0
  de WAITCNT), `dma_access_cycles()` y `dma_total_cycles()` suman el coste
  first/rest. El DMA ahora tambien alimenta a los timers con esos ciclos
  (`io_update_timers(g, dma_cyc)`), que es lo que GBATEK documenta: los timers
  siguen contando mientras el DMA tiene el bus.
- Efecto: `timing/dma_long` pasa de FAIL 001 a **PASS**. Los dos `DMA/DMA_ROM_*`
  cambian de codigo de fallo (009 -> 172/108) porque ahora el coste de ROM
  (WS0=4) se modela; siguen fallando por el resto del timing de pausa.
- `prefetcher/prefetcher_dma` deja de dar PASS **espurio**: leia TM0CNT_L y
